magisterium.assessment_en: It correctly emphasizes that Christian warfare is spiritual, not against people, and that disciples may face opposition because of fidelity to Christ. However, the absence of joy over another's spiritual good or the persecution of believers does not in itself allow for a certain conclusion that someone is "under the power of the evil one"; such a diagnosis is overly categorical.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Ephesians 6:12 calls Christians to distinguish spiritual warfare from hostility toward people, while Jesus' warning about fruits requires prudence, not hasty labeling. Persecution for fidelity to Christ is indeed a biblical reality, but it does not grant authority to impute to persecutors the ultimate state of their soul. Rejoicing in another's good is in accord with Christian charity; nevertheless, evaluating someone's guilt or spiritual state must remain humble and cautious.
concerns_en: Paul's statement that we do not wrestle against flesh and blood directs attention to the spiritual forces of evil, but does not justify sorting individual people into an enemy camp or concluding about their spiritual state.

Jesus' words about knowing them by their fruits call for prudent judgment, but the passage provides no basis for automatically declaring anyone who persecutes a person bearing fruit as being under the power of the evil one.

Not rejoicing in another's good may indicate envy or a lack of love, but from that, without additional discernment, it cannot be concluded that the person is under the power of the evil one; the wording can encourage unfounded judgment and fear.

sections.subtitle_en: The enemy is not human: how to recognize those under the power of the evil one
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains that we do not fight against human beings, but against evil spirits
sections.content_en:
The first point of the interpretation is that, according to Saint Paul, **we do not wrestle against flesh and blood, but against evil spirits**. The host warns that today many look upon people on the other side as enemies. The apostle, however, clearly says that the real struggle is spiritual. Under the power of the evil one, Grebenar explains, are many who are "of the world" and those who do not have the faith of the heart. All are subject to him, he adds, "more or less."

He then poses a crucial question: how does one recognize that someone is under the power of the evil one? He finds the answer in Jesus' words "by their fruits you shall know them." The one who **persecutes people who bear fruit for the kingdom of God** shows, according to the host, that he is under the power of the evil one. These can be people of the world who live in mortal sin, but also those who present themselves as believers, while in reality they are **"false brothers"**.

The host turns that thought toward the listeners themselves as well. Everyone should ask themselves whether perhaps they too stand on the side of false brothers. As a **test of faith**, he suggests a simple question: does a person rejoice in that which his Savior rejoices in? If someone feels no joy when hearing that a brother or sister has grown in faith, has been healed, or that their child has returned to church after drugs and alcohol, then, Grebenar warns, he is himself under the power of the evil one.

sections.subtitle: Idolatrija u novom ruhu: kad psihologija ili nogomet istisnu riječ Božju
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o vjernicima kojima je psihologija važnija od riječi Božje
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim upozorava na suptilniji oblik duhovnog zastranjivanja, onaj koji se događa i među praktičnim vjernicima. Navodi primjer osobe koja za sebe kaže da je vjernik, ide na svetu misu i živi sakramentalno, ali je **više zanima psihologija nego riječ Božja**. Za takav slučaj Grebenar odlučno kaže da je riječ o vlasti zloga i da „nema dileme o tome“.

Isto, nastavlja, vrijedi za svaku drugu stvar koja u životu zauzme prvo mjesto: **nogomet, košarka** ili bilo što drugo što čovjeku postane važnije od Božje riječi. Sve to naziva **idolatrijom**.

Kriterij koji nudi jednostavan je: ako čovjeka ne hrani riječ Božja, nego nešto drugo, i ako tom drugom daje prednost u životu, to dolazi od zloga. Vjernik se pritom može pozivati na to da je u Crkvi, ali voditelj takav pristup naziva „krivim metodama“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno upozorava da bilo koja stvorena stvar može postati idol ako zauzme Božje mjesto i postane čovjekova najviša odanost, ali neosnovano poistovjećuje veći interes za psihologiju ili sport s vlašću zloga. Katolički nauk razlikuje korištenje dobrih stvorenih stvari od njihova idoliziranja: presudno je postaju li apsolutne i potiskuju li Boga, a ne samo zanimaju li čovjeka više od čitanja Svetoga pisma.
concerns: Tvrdnja da „nema dileme” kako je veći interes za psihologiju od riječi Božje djelo zloga pripisuje duhovni uzrok bez dovoljno osnove; sama psihologija nije idol niti je nužno suprotstavljena vjeri.
Nogomet, košarka ili druga područja života nisu idolatrija sama po sebi. Postaju neuredna ako se apsolutiziraju i zbog njih se zanemaruju Bog, dužnosti prema bližnjima ili kršćanski život.

Kriterij da sve što čovjeka ne hrani riječju Božjom, nego nečim drugim, dolazi od zloga preširok je i ne razlikuje Sveto pismo kao temelj vjere od drugih dopuštenih izvora znanja, odmora i ljudskog rasta.
magisterium.enrichment: Ivan Pavao II. napominje da materijalne stvari mogu biti sredstva dobra, ali ne smiju zauzeti prvo mjesto u srcu; papa Franjo opisuje idolatriju kao vezanost koja postaje opsesija jačom od ljubavi prema Bogu i bližnjima. Stoga je prikladno ispitivati donosi li neka aktivnost zanemarivanje molitve, mise, obiteljskih obveza ili ljubavi prema bližnjemu, umjesto samu aktivnost proglasiti idolopoklonstvom.

citations.document_title: Pastoral Visit to the Ukraine: Meeting with young people in front of the Nativity of the Mother of God Church, at the Esplanade of Sykhiv, Lviv (June 26, 2001) - Speech

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly warns that any created thing can become an idol if it takes God's place and becomes man's highest devotion, but it baselessly equates greater interest in psychology or sports with the power of the evil one. Catholic teaching distinguishes using good created things from idolizing them: what is decisive is whether they become absolute and supplant God, and not merely whether they interest a person more than reading Sacred Scripture.
magisterium.enrichment_en: John Paul II notes that material things can be means of good, but must not take first place in the heart; Pope Francis describes idolatry as an attachment that becomes an obsession stronger than love for God and neighbors. Therefore, it is appropriate to examine whether an activity brings about neglect of prayer, Mass, family duties, or charity toward neighbor, instead of declaring the activity itself to be idolatry.
concerns_en: The claim that "there is no dilemma" that greater interest in psychology than the word of God is the work of the evil one attributes a spiritual cause without sufficient basis; psychology itself is not an idol nor is it necessarily opposed to faith.

Soccer, basketball, or other areas of life are not idolatry in themselves. They become disordered if they are absolutized and because of them God, duties toward neighbors, or Christian life are neglected.

The criterion that anything that does not feed a person with the word of God, but with something else, comes from the evil one is overly broad and does not distinguish Sacred Scripture as the foundation of faith from other permissible sources of knowledge, rest, and human growth.

sections.subtitle_en: Idolatry in new garb: when psychology or soccer displaces the word of God
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about believers to whom psychology is more important than the word of God
sections.content_en:
The host then warns of a subtler form of spiritual straying, one that occurs even among practicing believers. He cites the example of a person who says of himself that he is a believer, goes to Holy Mass, and lives sacramentally, but is **more interested in psychology than in the word of God**. For such a case, Grebenar decisively says that it is a matter of the power of the evil one and that "there is no dilemma about it."

The same, he continues, applies to every other thing that takes first place in life: **soccer, basketball**, or anything else that becomes more important to a person than God's word. He calls all of that **idolatry**.

The criterion he offers is simple: if a person is not nourished by the word of God, but by something else, and if he gives priority in life to that other thing, that comes from the evil one. A believer may appeal in doing so to being in the Church, but the host calls such an approach "wrong methods."

sections.subtitle: „Dan zli“: đavao nikad ne napada samo s jedne strane
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači pojam „dana zloga“ i napad s više strana istovremeno
sections.content:
Tumačeći Pavlov poziv da vjernici posegnu za **svom** opremom Božjom kako bi odoljeli „u dan zli“, voditelj objašnjava da apostol zna da će Sotona napadati one koji imaju vjeru „na sve moguće načine, na najperfidnije načine“. **Dan zli** je, kaže, dan koji je đavao sam odredio za napad.

Posebno naglašava da đavao **nikad ne napada samo s jedne strane, nego s više strana istovremeno**. Razlog je, prema Grebenaru, u tome što bi napad iz jednog smjera bilo lako razotkriti, pa zli napadom iz više smjerova zameće trag. Nadahne više ljudi pod svojom vlašću da napadaju, govore protiv nekoga i rade mu iza leđa, a da među njima uopće ne mora postojati nikakav dogovor.

Tu misao voditelj primjenjuje na aktualne događaje. Kad ljudi pitaju tko stoji iza političkih skupova i nereda u **Francuskoj** i koje udruge ili nevladine organizacije ih koordiniraju, on odgovara da iza toga stoji đavao. Priznaje da su neke organizacije možda i potaknule pokretanje, ali tvrdi da one nemaju toliki broj ljudi. Đavao, prema njegovu tumačenju, najprije nadahne jedne da nešto pokrenu, a zatim „podigne“ i mnoge koji nisu ni u kakvim organizacijama, nego se jednostavno uključe.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na svu Božju opremu i tvrdnja da se kršćani bore protiv duhovnih zlih sila imaju čvrst oslonac u Ef 6,11–18, a katolički nauk priznaje i djelovanje đavla u ljudskoj povijesti. Međutim, tvrdnje da đavao nikad ne napada samo s jedne strane, da sam određuje „dan zli” i da stoji iza konkretnih francuskih skupova i nereda predstavljene su kao sigurni zaključci, iako ih navedeni biblijski odlomak ne utvrđuje.
concerns: U Ef 6,13 „dan zli” nije opisan kao dan koji je đavao sam odredio; sveti Pavao poziva vjernike da se odupru zlu i ostanu postojani, dok tumačenje Ivana Zlatoustog taj izraz povezuje sa sadašnjim životom i potrebom trajne duhovne pripravnosti.

Biblijski tekst potvrđuje stvarnost duhovne borbe, ali ne kaže da đavao uvijek napada iz više smjerova istodobno niti da za to namjerno zameće trag. Takva kategorična tvrdnja nadilazi ono što odlomak podupire.

Pripisivanje konkretnih političkih skupova i nereda u Francuskoj đavlu bez razlučivanja i dokaza spekulativno je. Crkveno učenje upozorava na oprez pri pripisivanju pojedinih događaja izravnom djelovanju demona te istodobno čuva razliku između đavolskog poticaja i slobodne ljudske odgovornosti.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao poziva na istinu, pravednost, vjeru, spasenje, Božju riječ i ustrajnu molitvu; naglasak odlomka stoga je na kršćanskoj vjernosti, a ne na utvrđivanju tajnih uzročnika aktualnih događaja. Katolički nauk priznaje da đavao može iskušavati ljude jače ili šire od pojedinačnih slučajeva, ali naglašava da njegov utjecaj ne ukida ljudsku slobodu te da ljudi za svoja djela ostaju odgovorni. Zato je primjerenije govoriti o mogućem duhovnom utjecaju općenito, a konkretne političke tvrdnje procjenjivati na temelju provjerljivih činjenica.

citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)
Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

magisterium.assessment_en: The call to the whole armor of God and the assertion that Christians fight against spiritual forces of evil have a firm foundation in Eph 6:11–18, and Catholic teaching also recognizes the action of the devil in human history. However, the claims that the devil never attacks from only one side, that he himself determines the "evil day," and that he is behind the specific French rallies and riots are presented as certain conclusions, even though the cited biblical passage does not establish them.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul calls for truth, righteousness, faith, salvation, the Word of God, and persevering prayer; the emphasis of the passage is therefore on Christian fidelity, not on identifying hidden instigators of current events. Catholic teaching recognizes that the devil can tempt people more intensely or broadly than individual cases, but emphasizes that his influence does not abolish human freedom and that people remain responsible for their actions. Therefore, it is more appropriate to speak of possible spiritual influence in general, and evaluate concrete political claims based on verifiable facts.
concerns_en: In Eph 6:13, the "evil day" is not described as a day that the devil himself determined; Saint Paul calls believers to resist evil and remain steadfast, while John Chrysostom's interpretation links that expression to the present life and the need for ongoing spiritual readiness.

The biblical text confirms the reality of spiritual warfare, but does not say that the devil always attacks from multiple directions simultaneously, nor that he deliberately covers his tracks for that purpose. Such a categorical claim exceeds what the passage supports.

Attributing specific political rallies and riots in France to the devil without discernment and evidence is speculative. Church teaching warns of caution in attributing specific events to the direct action of demons, and simultaneously preserves the distinction between diabolical instigation and free human responsibility.

sections.subtitle_en: "The evil day": the devil never attacks from only one side
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the concept of the "evil day" and an attack from multiple sides simultaneously
sections.content_en:
Interpreting Paul's call for believers to take up **the whole** armor of God in order to withstand "in the evil day," the host explains that the apostle knows that Satan will attack those who have faith "in all possible ways, in the most perfidious ways." The **evil day** is, he says, a day that the devil himself has appointed for an attack.

He emphasizes in particular that the devil **never attacks from only one side, but from multiple sides simultaneously**. The reason, according to Grebenar, is that an attack from one direction would be easy to uncover, so the evil one covers his tracks by attacking from multiple directions. He inspires several people under his power to attack, speak against someone, and work behind their back, without there needing to be any agreement among them at all.

The host applies that thought to current events. When people ask who is behind political rallies and riots in **France** and which associations or non-governmental organizations coordinate them, he answers that the devil stands behind them. He concedes that some organizations may have initiated the launch, but claims that they do not possess such a number of people. The devil, according to his interpretation, first inspires some to launch something, and then "raises up" many who belong to no organizations at all, but simply join in.

sections.subtitle: Ubojstvo u Americi kao slika duhovne bolesti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj spominje ubojstvo Kirka u Americi i suđenje mladiću
sections.content:
Kao primjer onoga što može učiniti čovjek pod vlašću zloga, voditelj spominje **ubojstvo Kirka u Americi** i suđenje koje je u tijeku. Opisuje mladića koji je uzeo pušku sa snajperom, sakrio se i danima planirao ubojstvo, te se pita: koje je to nadahnuće?

Grebenaru je posebno upečatljiv dojam koji optuženi ostavlja na sudu. Djeluje racionalno i normalno, a zapravo je, kako kaže, **„duhovno bolestan“**. Smatra da je riječ o tolikoj duhovnoj pakosti i bolesti da netko danima čeka s puškom kako bi ubio čovjeka kojeg toliko mrzi, a da ga uopće ne poznaje.

Zaključak koji izvodi jest da se iz takvih postupaka vidi da je osoba pod vlašću zloga. Đavao, upozorava, ima svoje ljude kojima vlada i koji mogu napraviti isto i danas, pa i njemu osobno.

magisterium.assessment: Tvrdnja da zlo i đavao mogu poticati čovjeka na grijeh i nasilje u skladu je s katoličkim naukom, ali iz opisa optuženikova ponašanja ne može se pouzdano zaključiti da je „pod vlašću zloga” niti mu pripisati duhovnu bolest. Budući da je suđenje u tijeku, govor treba izbjegavati i pretpostavku krivnje i poistovjećivanje moguće psihičke bolesti s duhovnim zlom.
concerns: Izgleda da se iz ponašanja i dojma o optuženiku izvodi zaključak o njegovu duhovnom stanju i djelovanju đavla, premda katoličko učenje poziva na oprez pri takvoj prosudbi.

Izraz „duhovno bolestan” može zamagliti razliku između grijeha, duhovnog zla i moguće psihičke bolesti; samo naizgled racionalno ponašanje ne omogućuje dijagnozu ni siguran sud o moralnoj odgovornosti.
Opisivanje optuženika kao počinitelja prije završetka suđenja može ostaviti dojam da mu se unaprijed pripisuje krivnja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk priznaje da đavao napastuje i može moralno utjecati na čovjeka, ali grijeh ostaje ljudski čin: osoba na napast može slobodno pristati ili je odbiti, a đavao i ljudski grijeh nisu isto. Papa Pavao VI. izričito upozorava da svaki grijeh nije izravno posljedica đabolskog djelovanja te da procjena takvog djelovanja zahtijeva oprez; stoga je primjerenije osuditi ubojstvo kao teško zlo, a o krivnji i psihičkom stanju konkretne osobe govoriti bez preuranjenih zaključaka.

citations.document_author: Congregation for the Doctrine of the Faith

citations.document_title: Decisiones seu Sententiae, Tomus LXIII (Annus Decisionum: 1971)

magisterium.assessment_en: The claim that evil and the devil can incite a person to sin and violence is in accordance with Catholic teaching, but from the description of the defendant's behavior one cannot reliably conclude that he is "under the power of the evil one" nor attribute spiritual illness to him. Since the trial is ongoing, discourse should avoid both the presumption of guilt and equating potential mental illness with spiritual evil.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic doctrine recognizes that the devil tempts and can morally influence man, but sin remains a human act: a person can freely consent to temptation or reject it, and the devil and human sin are not the same thing. Pope Paul VI explicitly warns that not every sin is directly the consequence of diabolical action and that evaluating such action requires caution; therefore, it is more appropriate to condemn murder as a grave evil, and speak about the guilt and psychological state of the concrete person without premature conclusions.
concerns_en: It appears that from the behavior and impression of the defendant a conclusion is drawn about his spiritual state and the action of the devil, even though Catholic teaching calls for caution in such judgment.

The expression "spiritually ill" can blur the distinction between sin, spiritual evil, and possible mental illness; seemingly rational behavior alone does not enable a diagnosis or a certain judgment about moral responsibility.
Describing the defendant as the perpetrator before the conclusion of the trial can leave the impression that guilt is being attributed to him in advance.

sections.subtitle_en: Murder in America as an image of spiritual illness
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host mentions the murder of Kirk in America and the trial of the young man
sections.content_en:
As an example of what a person under the power of the evil one can do, the host mentions the **murder of Kirk in America** and the ongoing trial. He describes a young man who took a rifle with a sniper scope, hid, and planned the murder for days, and asks: what kind of inspiration is that?

Grebenar is particularly struck by the impression the accused makes in court. He appears rational and normal, but in reality is, as he says, **"spiritually ill"**. He considers that it is a matter of such spiritual malice and illness that someone waits for days with a rifle to kill a man whom he hates so much, without even knowing him at all.

The conclusion he draws is that such actions show that the person is under the power of the evil one. The devil, he warns, has his people whom he rules and who can do the same today, even to him personally.

sections.subtitle: Zaštita nije recitacija: oprema se mora razumjeti i živjeti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj naglašava da treba obući svu opremu Božju, a ne samo njezin dio
sections.content:
Na pitanje što je zaštita od napada zloga, voditelj odgovara da je to upravo ono o čemu govori sveti Pavao. Kad netko kaže „budi oprezan“, to u duhovnom smislu znači **obući svu opremu Božju**.

Naglasak stavlja na riječ **„svu“**: ne „neku“, nego cijelu opremu. Tko ide „na prvu liniju“, mora biti potpuno opremljen, inače će izgorjeti od ognjenih strijela zloga. Kritizira i naviku da se taj biblijski tekst samo čita kao zaštitna molitva i „izrecitira“, bez razumijevanja. Smatra da je nužno znati što svaki dio opreme znači.

Razlog za stalnu opremljenost objašnjava jednostavno: čovjek ne zna kada je đavao odlučio udariti svom silom. Zato oprema Božja treba biti na njemu stalno, kako bi se u tom trenutku mogao oduprijeti.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s Ef 6, gdje Pavao izričito poziva kršćane da obuku svu Božju opremu kako bi se oduprli đavolskim zamkama, te opravdano upozorava da se taj odlomak ne svede na nerazumljivo recitiranje. Ipak, formulacija o udaru zloga „svom silom” može zvučati kao da je kršćanski život prvenstveno obilježen strahom, što treba uravnotežiti pouzdanjem u Boga i konkretnim značenjem pojedinih dijelova opreme.
concerns: Naglasak na nepredvidivom trenutku kada će đavao napasti može poticati pretjeranu tjeskobu ili dojam da je oprema zaštitna formula. Pavao poziva na budnost i ustrajnu molitvu, ali oprema je slikovit prikaz života u istini, pravednosti, vjeri, evanđelju i Božjoj riječi, a ne čarobni postupak.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao objašnjava da oprema uključuje pojas istine, oklop pravednosti, spremnost za evanđelje mira, štit vjere, kacigu spasenja i mač Duha, odnosno Božju riječ; odmah zatim traži molitvu i budnost za sve svete. Zato „obući svu opremu” znači živjeti cjelovit kršćanski život, a ne samo izgovoriti određeni tekst: crkveni nauk kao sredstva duhovne borbe navodi i molitvu, Božju riječ, misu, sakramentalno pomirenje, djela ljubavi i život zajednice.

citations.document_author: The New Revised Standard Version, Catholic Edition (NRSV-CE)

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Eph 6, where Paul explicitly calls Christians to put on the whole armor of God in order to stand against the wiles of the devil, and it rightly warns against reducing that passage to an uncomprehending recitation. Still, the formulation about the evil one striking "with all his might" can sound as though Christian life is primarily marked by fear, which must be balanced by trust in God and the concrete meaning of individual pieces of the armor.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul explains that the armor includes the belt of truth, the breastplate of righteousness, readiness for the gospel of peace, the shield of faith, the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the Word of God; immediately following, he asks for prayer and vigilance for all the saints. Therefore, "putting on the whole armor" means living a comprehensive Christian life, and not just reciting a particular text: Church teaching lists prayer, the Word of God, Mass, sacramental reconciliation, works of charity, and community life as means of spiritual warfare.
concerns_en: The emphasis on the unpredictable moment when the devil will attack can foster excessive anxiety or the impression that the armor is a protective formula. Paul calls for vigilance and persevering prayer, but the armor is a vivid depiction of living in truth, righteousness, faith, the Gospel, and the Word of God, not a magical procedure.

sections.subtitle_en: Protection is not recitation: armor must be understood and lived
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host emphasizes that one must put on the whole armor of God, not just part of it
sections.content_en:
To the question of what constitutes protection against attacks by the evil one, the host answers that it is precisely what Saint Paul speaks of. When someone says "be careful," in a spiritual sense that means **putting on the whole armor of God**.

He places emphasis on the word **"whole"**: not "some," but the entire armor. Whoever goes "to the front line" must be fully equipped, otherwise he will burn from the flaming darts of the evil one. He also criticizes the habit of merely reading that biblical text as a protective prayer and "reciting" it, without understanding. He considers it necessary to know what each piece of armor means.

He explains the reason for constant readiness simply: a person does not know when the devil has decided to strike with all his might. That is why the armor of God needs to be on him constantly, so that at that moment he can resist.

sections.subtitle: Istina s velikim slovom: zašto „istinito“ nije isto što i „istina“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava razliku između istine i onoga što je istinito
sections.content:
Prvi dio opreme, **opasati bedra istinom**, voditelj tumači kao poziv da se okolina, svijet i događaji promatraju drugačije nego što ih tumače ljudi. Kao primjer navodi aktualne događaje: nemire u Francuskoj i Srbiji, političke komentatore koji ih objašnjavaju, te skandiranje dijela navijača Torcide koji zazivaju Hitlera. Pritom naglašava da je riječ o manjem dijelu ljudi, a ne o čitavoj navijačkoj skupini.

Za sve to, kaže, postoje tumačenja koja su **„istinita“**: istinito je da društvo nije do kraja uređeno, da je Vučić bio diktator i ratni huškač, da u Francuskoj pada standard pa su ljudi nezadovoljni. To su argumenti koji se racionalno mogu braniti. No Grebenar inzistira da **„istina“ i „istinito“ nisu isti pojmovi**. Istinito je ono što ljudi tumače.

Razliku ilustrira primjerima:

- **rat u Bosni i Hercegovini**: tri naroda, tri tumačenja onoga što se dogodilo;
- **Drugi svjetski rat**: različita tumačenja;
- **današnji događaji**: isti događaj, a različita tumačenja.

Svaka strana iznosi istinite argumente, ali samo one koji joj odgovaraju. Mnogo toga se prešuti, pa se istina ne može spoznati. **Istina je samo jedna**, to je ono što se zaista dogodilo, a Isus je onaj koji sve osvjetljava. Opasati bedra istinom znači, zaključuje voditelj, promatrati svijet po istini „koja se piše velikim slovima“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s katoličkim naukom jer odbacuje relativizam, priznaje da se događaji ne mogu svesti na jednostrane prikaze i povezuje puninu istine s Isusom Kristom; Pavao doista poziva vjernike da se opasuju istinom. Ipak, razlikovanje „istine“ od „istinitoga“ ostaje nejasno i može zvučati kao da su istinite tvrdnje tek subjektivna tumačenja, dok je za katolički nauk istina i vjernost Bogu i podudaranje razuma sa stvarnošću.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je „istinito ono što ljudi tumače“ nije dovoljno precizna: ljudi mogu iznijeti istinite ili djelomično istinite tvrdnje, ali istinitost ne nastaje njihovim tumačenjem; ona ovisi o tome odgovara li sud stvarnosti.

Primjeri rata i političkih događaja traže razliku između samih činjenica, njihova tumačenja i prešućivanja. To što različite strane nude djelomično istinite argumente ne znači da su sva tumačenja jednako valjana niti da se istina o događaju ne može spoznati.

Izraz „istina je samo jedna, to je ono što se zaista dogodilo“ prikladan je za naglašavanje objektivne stvarnosti, ali može suziti pojam istine na povijesne činjenice. Kršćanska istina uključuje i Božju vjernost i objavljenu istinu, a punina je osobno objavljena u Kristu.
Biblijski stih o pojasu istine podupire poziv na vjernost istini, ali sam po sebi ne utvrđuje da je tumačenje svih suvremenih političkih događaja smisao Pavlove slike.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički govor o istini obuhvaća i vjernost: Bog je istinit jer ostaje vjeran svojoj riječi, a čovjek je pozvan živjeti i govoriti istinito; obuhvaća i istinitost prosudbi, koje su istinite kada odgovaraju stvarnosti. Zato različita tumačenja treba provjeravati razlozima i činjenicama, a ne zaključiti da su sva podjednako istinita; vjera i razum zajedno služe traženju istine. Krist je za kršćane više od mjerila za procjenu događaja: on je osobno utjelovljena punina istine, pa se traženje istine povezuje s nasljedovanjem njegove vjernosti i ljubavi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with Catholic teaching because it rejects relativism, recognizes that events cannot be reduced to one-sided depictions, and connects the fullness of truth with Jesus Christ; Paul indeed calls believers to gird their loins with truth. Nevertheless, the distinction between "truth" and "what is true" remains unclear and may sound as though true claims are merely subjective interpretations, whereas for Catholic teaching truth is both fidelity to God and the conformity of intellect with reality.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic discourse on truth also encompasses fidelity: God is true because he remains faithful to his word, and man is called to live and speak truthfully; it also encompasses the truth of judgments, which are true when they correspond to reality. Therefore, different interpretations should be verified by reasons and facts, rather than concluding that all are equally true; faith and reason together serve the search for truth. For Christians, Christ is more than a standard for evaluating events: he is personally the incarnate fullness of truth, so the pursuit of truth is linked with imitating his fidelity and love.
concerns_en: The assertion that "what is true is what people interpret" is not sufficiently precise: people can put forward true or partially true claims, but truth does not arise from their interpretation; it depends on whether the judgment corresponds to reality.

The examples of war and political events require a distinction between the facts themselves, their interpretation, and omissions. The fact that different sides offer partially true arguments does not mean that all interpretations are equally valid or that the truth about an event cannot be known.

The expression "there is only one truth, that is what really happened" is suitable for emphasizing objective reality, but it can narrow the concept of truth to historical facts. Christian truth also includes God's fidelity and revealed truth, and its fullness is personally revealed in Christ.
The biblical verse about the belt of truth supports the call to fidelity to truth, but in itself does not establish that interpreting all contemporary political events is the meaning of Paul's image.

sections.subtitle_en: Truth with a capital letter: why "truthful" is not the same as "truth"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains the difference between truth and what is truthful
sections.content_en:
The first piece of armor, **girding the loins with truth**, the host interprets as a call to view the environment, the world, and events differently from how people interpret them. As an example, he cites current events: riots in France and Serbia, political commentators explaining them, and the chanting of a portion of Torcida fans invoking Hitler. In doing so, he emphasizes that this involves a smaller segment of people, and not the entire fan group.

For all of this, he says, there are interpretations that are **"truthful"**: it is truthful that society is not completely ordered, that Vučić was a dictator and warmonger, that in France living standards are falling so people are dissatisfied. These are arguments that can be rationally defended. But Grebenar insists that **"truth" and "truthful" are not the same concepts**. Truthful is what people interpret.

He illustrates the difference with examples:

- the **war in Bosnia and Herzegovina**: three peoples, three interpretations of what happened;
- **World War II**: differing interpretations;
- **today's events**: the same event, but different interpretations.

Each side presents truthful arguments, but only those that suit it. Much is concealed in silence, so the truth cannot be known. **The truth is only one**, that is what truly happened, and Jesus is the one who illuminates everything. Girding the loins with truth means, the host concludes, observing the world according to the truth "that is written with capital letters."

sections.subtitle: Francuski nemiri u svjetlu napuštanja Boga
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači prosvjede u Francuskoj kao posljedicu napuštanja Boga
sections.content:
Kao primjer tumačenja događaja „po istini“, voditelj nudi svoje viđenje uzroka prosvjeda u Francuskoj. Smatra da su izbili **zato što su Francuzi napustili Boga**.

Prema njegovu tumačenju, Francuzi su dopustili da njihovu djecu odgajaju, kako kaže, „radikalno lijevi“ ljudi, koji ih uče da je normalno da muškarac i muškarac imaju spolne odnose i da mogu imati dijete. Kad indoktrinirani učitelji tako odgajaju mlade, oni u odrasloj dobi postaju destruktivni i sve uništavaju. Grebenar tu povezuje neprirodno učenje s neprirodnim ponašanjem: tko je učen „neprirodnim pojavama“, i sam se tako ponaša.

To je za njega primjer onoga što znači „opasati bedra istinom“: tumačiti i razumijevati događaje oko sebe uvijek **kroz riječ Božju, koja je istina**.

magisterium.assessment: Tvrdnja da su homoseksualni spolni čini protivni katoličkom moralnom nauku jest usklađena s naukom Crkve, ali odlomak zatim iznosi nedokazanu tvrdnju da su francuski prosvjedi posljedica napuštanja Boga i odgoja mladih od strane „radikalno lijevih“ učitelja. Takvo svođenje složenih društvenih događaja na jednu uzročnu priču i njihovo pripisivanje skupinama ljudi nije opravdano Efežanima 6, koji govori o duhovnoj borbi, a ne nudi metodu za utvrđivanje uzroka konkretnih prosvjeda.
concerns: Odlomak ne pruža dokaze da su prosvjedi izbili zbog napuštanja Boga niti da ih uzrokuje određena vrsta učitelja; takvu tvrdnju ne treba predstavljati kao zaključak koji proizlazi iz katoličke vjere.

Veza između navodnog „neprirodnog učenja“ i toga da mladi u odrasloj dobi postaju destruktivni široka je i stigmatizirajuća generalizacija, bez potpore u navedenom biblijskom tekstu ili katoličkom nauku.
Katolički nauk moralno prosuđuje određene spolne čine, ali zahtijeva poštovanje, suosjećanje i osjetljivost prema osobama s homoseksualnim sklonostima te izbjegavanje nepravedne diskriminacije.
Izraz da muškarac i muškarac „mogu imati dijete“ nije dovoljno precizan: katoličko učenje razlikuje roditeljstvo od biološke sposobnosti dviju osoba istoga spola da zajednički začnu dijete.
magisterium.enrichment: Efežanima 6,10–18 opisuje „opremu Božju“ kao istinu, pravednost, naviještanje evanđelja mira, vjeru, spasenje, Božju riječ i molitvu; tekst poziva na vjernost i postojanost, ne na neutemeljeno pripisivanje krivnje za društvene nemire. Crkva uči da homoseksualni čini ne odgovaraju njezinu razumijevanju spolnosti i braka, ali istodobno jasno traži da se osobe ne svode na svoju sklonost i da se prema njima postupa s poštovanjem i bez nepravedne diskriminacije.

magisterium.assessment_en: The assertion that homosexual sexual acts are contrary to Catholic moral teaching is aligned with the teaching of the Church, but the passage then puts forward the unproven assertion that the French protests are the consequence of abandoning God and the upbringing of youth by "radical left" teachers. Such a reduction of complex social events to a single causal narrative and attributing them to groups of people is not justified by Ephesians 6, which speaks of spiritual warfare and does not offer a method for establishing the causes of specific protests.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Ephesians 6:10–18 describes the "armor of God" as truth, righteousness, proclamation of the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, the Word of God, and prayer; the text calls for fidelity and steadfastness, not for unfounded attribution of guilt for social unrest. The Church teaches that homosexual acts do not correspond to its understanding of sexuality and marriage, but at the same time clearly demands that persons not be reduced to their inclinations and that they be treated with respect, compassion, and sensitivity without unjust discrimination.
concerns_en: The passage provides no evidence that the protests erupted because of abandoning God or that they were caused by a certain type of teachers; such a claim should not be presented as a conclusion that follows from the Catholic faith.
The link between alleged "unnatural teaching" and youth becoming destructive in adulthood is a broad and stigmatizing generalization, without support in the cited biblical text or Catholic doctrine.
Catholic teaching morally evaluates certain sexual acts, but requires respect, compassion, and sensitivity toward persons with homosexual inclinations and the avoidance of unjust discrimination.

The expression that a man and a man "can have a child" is not sufficiently precise: Catholic teaching distinguishes parenthood from the biological capacity of two persons of the same sex to jointly conceive a child.

sections.subtitle_en: French riots in light of abandoning God
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the protests in France as a consequence of abandoning God
sections.content_en:
As an example of interpreting events "according to the truth," the host offers his view of the causes of the protests in France. He considers that they broke out **because the French abandoned God**.

According to his interpretation, the French allowed their children to be raised by, as he says, "radical left" people, who teach them that it is normal for a man and a man to have sexual relations and that they can have a child. When indoctrinated teachers raise young people like that, they become destructive in adulthood and destroy everything. Grebenar here connects unnatural teaching with unnatural behavior: whoever is taught "unnatural phenomena" behaves that way himself.

For him, that is an example of what it means to "gird the loins with truth": always interpreting and understanding the events around oneself **through the word of God, which is truth**.

sections.subtitle: Oklop pravednosti: težak teret koji daje sam Bog
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj svjedoči o viđenju u molitvi u kojem mu anđeo stavlja oklop pravednosti
sections.content:
Drugi dio opreme je **oklop pravednosti**. Voditelj podsjeća da Sveto pismo pravednikom naziva onoga **koji vrši volju Božju**. Ističe da je oklop težak i da vršiti volju Božju nije lako, ali da Bog štiti one koji je vrše. Kako je, kaže, više puta ponovio, čim čovjek krene vršiti volju Božju, Bog šalje anđele i svete i daje mnogo veću zaštitu njemu i njegovu domu.

Ključno je, naglašava Grebenar, da **čovjek taj oklop ne može obući sam, nego mu ga Bog mora dati**. Na to se nadovezuje osobnim svjedočanstvom. U jednoj molitvi, dok je razmatrao, vidio je kako je Gospodin zapovjedio jednom anđelu da na njega stavi oklop pravednosti. Tu zaštitu povezuje s time što je pristao činiti nešto na što ga je pozvao Duh Sveti, i kaže da otada osjeća veliku zaštitu.

Težinu tog oklopa slikovito opisuje uspomenom iz djetinjstva, kad je jednom obukao pancirku koja štiti od metaka i osjetio koliko je teška. Tako je i s duhovnim oklopom: čovjek čini ono što sam ne želi, a ljudi bi se tereta najradije oslobodili. Zapovjednik koji daje taj oklop jest Isus. On zapovijeda da se onaj koji vrši njegovu svetu volju obuče u oklop pravednosti.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje uglavnom odgovara Ef 6, gdje Pavao poziva vjernike da obuku „oklop pravednosti” i cijelu Božju opremu kako bi se oduprli zlu; povezati pravednost s vršenjem Božje volje razumno je, premda pravednost obuhvaća širi život kreposti i djelovanje milosti. Naglasak da je zaštita Božji dar dobro je utemeljen, ali tvrdnja da poslušnost Božjoj volji pouzdano donosi posebnu zaštitu anđela pojedincu i njegovu domu nadilazi ono što ovaj biblijski odlomak izričito obećava.
concerns: Tvrdnja da Bog čim čovjek krene vršiti njegovu volju šalje anđele i svece te daje „mnogo veću zaštitu” zvuči kao opće, zajamčeno obećanje. Ef 6 govori o Božjoj opremi za duhovnu borbu, ali ne jamči da će vjernik ili njegov dom biti pošteđeni nevolja; takvo osobno svjedočanstvo valja prikazati kao osobno iskustvo, a ne kao opće pravilo.
Viđenje anđela koji stavlja oklop može se iznijeti kao osobno iskustvo molitve, ali samo po sebi nije dokaz nauka niti ga treba poistovjetiti s objavljenom istinom.

Izraz da je pravednik onaj koji vrši Božju volju koristan je, ali može zvučati kao da pravednost čovjek stječe samo vlastitim naporom. Kršćanska pravednost također je Božji dar i plod milosti, na koji čovjek odgovara životom vjere, kreposti i ljubavi.
magisterium.enrichment: U Ef 6,10–18 oklop je Božji, a vjernici su istodobno pozvani da ga obuku: slika zato povezuje Božju pomoć s ljudskom budnošću, ustrajnošću, molitvom i vjernim životom. Tumačenje sv. Ivana Zlatoustoga opisuje oklop pravednosti kao život sveopće kreposti, dok teološko tumačenje pravednost u Kristu povezuje s darom Božjim i odgovorom ljubavi, a ne samo s naporom da se izvrše zapovijedi.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation mainly corresponds to Eph 6, where Paul calls believers to put on the "breastplate of righteousness" and the whole armor of God to resist evil; linking righteousness with doing God's will is reasonable, although righteousness encompasses a broader life of virtue and the action of grace. The emphasis that protection is God's gift is well-grounded, but the claim that obedience to God's will reliably brings special protection of angels to an individual and his home goes beyond what this biblical passage explicitly promises.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Eph 6:10–18, the armor is God's, and believers are simultaneously called to put it on: the image therefore links God's help with human vigilance, perseverance, prayer, and faithful life. Saint John Chrysostom's interpretation describes the breastplate of righteousness as a life of universal virtue, while theological interpretation links righteousness in Christ with the gift of God and a response of love, not merely with the effort to carry out commandments.
concerns_en: The claim that as soon as a person starts doing God's will, God sends angels and saints and provides "much greater protection" sounds like a general, guaranteed promise. Eph 6 speaks of the armor of God for spiritual warfare, but does not guarantee that the believer or his home will be spared from afflictions; such personal testimony should be presented as personal experience, and not as a general rule.
The vision of an angel placing armor can be presented as a personal prayer experience, but in itself is not proof of doctrine nor should it be equated with revealed truth.

The expression that a righteous person is one who does God's will is useful, but can sound as though righteousness is acquired solely by human effort. Christian righteousness is also God's gift and the fruit of grace, to which man responds with a life of faith, virtue, and love.

sections.subtitle_en: Breastplate of righteousness: a heavy burden given by God Himself
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host testifies to a vision in prayer in which an angel places the breastplate of righteousness upon him
sections.content_en:
The second piece of armor is the **breastplate of righteousness**. The host recalls that Sacred Scripture calls righteous the one **who does the will of God**. He points out that the armor is heavy and that doing the will of God is not easy, but that God protects those who do it. As he has, he says, repeated several times, as soon as a person begins to do the will of God, God sends angels and saints and gives much greater protection to him and his home.

The crucial point, Grebenar emphasizes, is that **a person cannot put on that armor by himself, but God must give it to him**. To this he attaches personal testimony. In one prayer, while he was meditating, he saw how the Lord commanded an angel to place the breastplate of righteousness upon him. He connects that protection with having agreed to do something to which the Holy Spirit called him, and says that since then he has felt great protection.

He vividly describes the weight of that armor with a childhood memory, when he once put on a bulletproof vest that protects against bullets and felt how heavy it was. So it is with spiritual armor: a person does what he himself does not wish, and people would most gladly free themselves of the burden. The commander who gives that armor is Jesus. He commands that the one who does his holy will be clothed in the breastplate of righteousness.

sections.subtitle: Spremnost bez odgađanja: Božje stvari na prvo mjesto u danu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira „bljutavu vjeru“ onih koji odgađaju Božji poziv
sections.content:
Pod onim što je u čovjekovoj moći, a to je želja da vrši volju Božju, voditelj tumači treći dio opreme: **potpasati noge spremnošću za evanđelje mira**. Pita tko je imao obuću svezanu na nogama i odgovara: Židovi, kad su blagovali Pashu i bili spremni na pokret. **Ključna riječ je spremnost**. Pritom citira svetog Ignacija, koji poziva na brzu spremnost, i Isusa, koji kaže: „odmah“.

Grebenar opisuje čest razgovor s ljudima koji su primili poziv, ali ne kreću jer „imaju još posla“ i moraju nešto završiti. Takav stav naziva **mlitavim i „bljutavom vjerom“**. Kod Gospodina toga nema: kad on pozove i da zadatak, taj zadatak je na prvom mjestu.

Upozorava na čestu pojavu: ljudi se uključe u služenje Gospodinu, primjerice vode neki projekt ili su članovi projektnog tima, ali taj zadatak stave „na deseto mjesto u danu“. Najprije posao, pa obitelj, pa sve ostalo, a tek navečer, umorni, posvete se onome Božjem. Voditelj poziva na suprotan redoslijed, pozivajući se na riječi „tražite najprije kraljevstvo Božje i sve ostalo će vam se nadodati“. Savjetuje da se ujutro najprije radi ono što je Božje, pa ako treba doći ranije na posao, odraditi posao i navečer otići na svetu misu.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na spremnosti za naviještanje evanđelja i prvenstvu Božjega kraljevstva uglavnom je u skladu s Ef 6,15 i Mt 6,33, a crkveno učenje također potiče odlučno prihvaćanje Božjega poziva. Ipak, poruku o „prvom mjestu u danu” treba razumjeti kao prvenstvo Boga u cjelokupnom životu, a ne kao krut raspored ili razlog za zanemarivanje obiteljskih i radnih dužnosti.
concerns: Savjet da se ujutro najprije radi ono „Božje” može zvučati kao da su posao i obitelj manje važni ili odvojeni od služenja Bogu; katoličko razumijevanje prvenstva Kraljevstva obuhvaća i odgovorno izvršavanje svakodnevnih dužnosti.
Nazivanje vjere „mlitavom” ili „bljutavom” zbog odgađanja može biti pretjerano ako se ne uzmu u obzir legitimne obveze, razborito razlučivanje i stvarna ograničenja osobe.
magisterium.enrichment: U Ef 6,15 obuća označava spremnost da se naviješta evanđelje mira, a ne naprosto brzinu u izvršavanju bilo kojeg zadatka; papa Franjo povezuje tu spremnost s apostolskim žarom i kretanjem u susret drugima. Isusove riječi „tražite najprije kraljevstvo Božje” određuju prvenstvo Boga i njegove pravednosti, ali ne nalažu da se zanemare posao ili obitelj. Rad i svakodnevne odgovornosti mogu se uključiti u traženje Kraljevstva, dok se konkretni pozivi trebaju živjeti razborito i u skladu s dužnostima prema bližnjima.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on readiness to proclaim the Gospel and the primacy of the Kingdom of God is mainly in alignment with Eph 6:15 and Mt 6:33, and Church teaching also encourages decisive acceptance of God's call. Nevertheless, the message about the "first place in the day" should be understood as the primacy of God in one's entire life, rather than as a rigid schedule or a reason to neglect family and work duties.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Eph 6:15 footwear signifies readiness to proclaim the gospel of peace, and not simply speed in executing any task; Pope Francis connects this readiness with apostolic zeal and setting out to encounter others. Jesus' words "seek first the Kingdom of God" establish the primacy of God and his righteousness, but do not prescribe neglecting work or family. Work and daily responsibilities can be integrated into seeking the Kingdom, while specific calls should be lived prudently and in accordance with duties toward neighbors.
concerns_en: The advice that in the morning one should first do what is "God's" can sound as though work and family are less important or separate from serving God; the Catholic understanding of the primacy of the Kingdom encompasses the responsible execution of daily duties as well.
Calling faith "flabby" or "insipid" due to delay can be exaggerated if legitimate obligations, prudent discernment, and a person's real limitations are not taken into account.

sections.subtitle_en: Readiness without delay: God's things in first place during the day
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host criticizes the "lukewarm faith" of those who delay God's call
sections.content_en:
Under what is within man's power, which is the desire to do the will of God, the host interprets the third piece of armor: **shodding feet with the preparation of the gospel of peace**. He asks who had shoes tied on their feet and answers: the Jews, when they ate the Passover and were ready to move. **The key word is readiness**. In doing so, he cites Saint Ignatius, who calls for swift readiness, and Jesus, who says: "immediately."

Grebenar describes a frequent conversation with people who have received a call, but do not set out because "they still have work" and have to finish something. Such an attitude he calls **sluggish and "lukewarm faith"**. With the Lord there is none of that: when He calls and gives an assignment, that assignment is in first place.

He warns of a common phenomenon: people get involved in serving the Lord, for example leading a project or being members of a project team, but put that task "in tenth place in the day." First work, then family, then everything else, and only in the evening, tired, do they devote themselves to what is God's. The host calls for the opposite order, appealing to the words "seek first the kingdom of God and all the rest will be added unto you." He advises doing what is God's first in the morning, and if necessary arriving earlier at work, finishing the work, and in the evening going to Holy Mass.

sections.subtitle: Štit vjere je povjerenje: kako sumnja razara zajednice
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj iznosi iskustvo s članovima inicijative koji su odustali zbog posijane sumnje
sections.content:
Četvrti dio opreme, **štit vjere**, voditelj tumači kao **povjerenje u Boga** i odnos povjerenja među ljudima. Objašnjava ga svakodnevnim primjerom: kad netko prenese glasinu o nekoj osobi, a ti odgovoriš „poznajem tog čovjeka, imam toliko iskustava s njim, ne vjerujem da je to rekao ili učinio“. Takvo se povjerenje, naglašava, **izgrađuje kroz duge godine**.

Štit vjere znači i odmah odbaciti herezu, ali i ne nasjesti kad netko u molitvenoj zajednici „rovari“ protiv voditelja ili kad netko u firmi podmeće lideru. On štiti od sumnje koju sije zli. Grebenar podsjeća da je đavao od početka nastupao upravo sumnjom: Isusu je rekao „ako si Sin Božji“, a Adamu i Evi „zar vam je Bog rekao“. Tako đavao razara Božje djelo. Sumnju posije preko nekoga tko djeluje kao autoritet.

Voditelj to potkrepljuje **iskustvom iz domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora**. Netko se učlani, oduševljeno o tome priča nekome drugome, a taj ga odgovara: „Nemoj ni slučajno, znaš što govore o njima.“ Osoba povjeruje, u srcu se rodi sumnja i, kako kaže Grebenar, „čim se sumnja rodi, gotovo je“. Slijedi kratak e-mail, „neću više, izlazim“, bez ikakva objašnjenja. Bog dopušta, smatra voditelj, da tako otpadnu oni koji nemaju štit vjere.

Naglašava da se **bez povjerenja ništa ne može graditi**. To ilustrira brakom u kojem jedan supružnik prevari drugoga i poslovnim partnerstvom u kojem partner uzme novac i odbaci te. Uzeti štit vjere znači izgraditi tako jako povjerenje u Boga i Crkvu, u ono što Crkva autentično uči, da čovjeka nitko ne može okrenuti na hinduizam, budizam, islam ili druge hereze.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje ispravno povezuje štit vjere s pouzdanjem u Boga i zaštitom od duhovnih napasti, što odgovara Ef 6,16, ali ga neopravdano sužava na povjerenje u osobe i voditelje te na odbacivanje sumnje bez razlučivanja. Tvrdnja da je čim se sumnja pojavi sve gotovo, kao i zaključak da oni koji napuste inicijativu nemaju štit vjere, pretjerani su i mogu poticati neosnovano nepovjerenje prema opravdanim pitanjima ili kritikama.
concerns: Štit vjere u Ef 6,16 primarno označava vjeru koja štiti od napada zloga, a ne bezuvjetno povjerenje u ljudske vođe ili organizacije; prenošenje te slike na ljudske odnose ne smije zamijeniti razborito provjeravanje glasina i postupaka.

Potrebno je razlikovati sumnju koja odbacuje vjeru od iskrenog traženja razloga, propitivanja ili razmatranja prigovora: Newman izričito razlikuje istraživanje temelja vjere od stvarne sumnje i dopušta razmatranje argumenata protiv nje kada za to postoji dobar razlog.

Zaključak da je nečiji odlazak iz inicijative dokaz nedostatka štita vjere pripisuje duhovni uzrok bez dovoljno osnove, a formulacija da se sumnja rodi pa je gotovo zanemaruje mogućnost razboritog razlučivanja i razgovora.
Islam, hinduizam i budizam nisu, u strogom teološkom smislu, kršćanske hereze; hereza se odnosi na tvrdokorno poricanje ili sumnju u istinu koja se vjerom treba vjerovati nakon krštenja.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao kaže, „uzmite uza se štit vjere“ kako biste mogli ugasiti ognjene strijele Zloga; slika naglašava oslonac na Boga u kušnjama, a ne imunitet ljudskih autoriteta od provjere. Ivan Zlatousti također povezuje štit s vjerom koja čuva vjernika u opasnostima i napastima. Katolička vjernost Crkvi zato se može spojiti s poštenim ispitivanjem konkretnih tvrdnji i postupaka, bez poistovjećivanja svake kritike s napadom zloga ili s odbacivanjem vjere.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation correctly connects the shield of faith with trust in God and protection from spiritual temptations, which corresponds to Eph 6:16, but baselessly narrows it to trust in persons and leaders and to rejecting doubt without discernment. The assertion that as soon as doubt appears everything is over, as well as the conclusion that those who leave an initiative do not have the shield of faith, are exaggerated and can encourage unfounded mistrust toward legitimate questions or criticisms.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul says, "take the shield of faith" so that you can extinguish the flaming darts of the Evil One; the image emphasizes reliance on God in trials, not the immunity of human authorities from scrutiny. John Chrysostom likewise connects the shield with faith that protects the believer in perils and temptations. Catholic fidelity to the Church can therefore be combined with honest examination of specific claims and actions, without equating every critique with an attack by the evil one or with a rejection of faith.
concerns_en: The shield of faith in Eph 6:16 primarily denotes faith that protects against the attacks of the evil one, not unconditional trust in human leaders or organizations; transferring that image to human relationships must not replace prudent verification of rumors and actions.

It is necessary to distinguish doubt that rejects faith from sincere inquiry for reasons, questioning, or considering objections: Newman explicitly distinguishes investigating the grounds of faith from real doubt and allows considering arguments against it when there is good reason to do so.

The conclusion that someone's departure from an initiative is proof of lacking the shield of faith attributes a spiritual cause without sufficient basis, and the phrasing that once doubt is born it is over ignores the possibility of prudent discernment and dialogue.

Islam, Hinduism, and Buddhism are not, in the strict theological sense, Christian heresies; heresy refers to the obstinate post-baptismal denial or doubt of some truth that must be believed with divine and Catholic faith.

sections.subtitle_en: The shield of faith is trust: how doubt destroys communities
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host presents an experience with members of the initiative who gave up due to sown doubt
sections.content_en:
The fourth piece of armor, the **shield of faith**, the host interprets as **trust in God** and a relationship of trust among people. He explains it with an everyday example: when someone passes on a rumor about a person, and you answer "I know that person, I have so many experiences with him, I don't believe he said or did that." Such trust, he emphasizes, **is built up through long years**.

The shield of faith also means immediately rejecting heresy, but also not falling for it when someone in a prayer community "undermines" the leader or when someone in a company undermines a manager. It protects from the doubt sown by the evil one. Grebenar recalls that from the beginning the devil operated precisely with doubt: he said to Jesus "if you are the Son of God," and to Adam and Eve "did God really say." In this way the devil destroys God's work. He sows doubt through someone who appears as an authority.

The host substantiates this with **experience from the patriotic initiative Ora et Labora**. Someone joins, enthusiastically speaks about it to someone else, and that other person talks him out of it: "Don't you dare, you know what they say about them." The person believes it, doubt is born in the heart, and, as Grebenar says, "as soon as doubt is born, it's over." A brief email follows, "I'm out, I'm quitting," without any explanation. God allows, the host considers, those who do not have the shield of faith to fall away like that.

He emphasizes that **without trust nothing can be built**. He illustrates this with a marriage in which one spouse cheats on the other, and a business partnership in which a partner takes the money and discards you. Taking the shield of faith means building such strong trust in God and the Church, in what the Church authentically teaches, that no one can turn a person toward Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, or other heresies.

sections.subtitle: Sumnja kao najjače đavolje oružje koje rađa izdaju
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o sumnji kao izvoru izdaje i spominje Danteov deveti krug pakla
sections.content:
Đavolje **ognjene strijele**, objašnjava voditelj, usmjerene su upravo na to da se posije sumnja. Nižu se pitanja: „Zar vam je Bog rekao?“, „Ako si Sin Božji“, „Zar si se ti učlanio u tu zajednicu? Znaš li što o njima govore?“ Čim netko tako govori, kaže Grebenar, to dolazi od đavla.

Sumnja, nastavlja, **rađa izdaju**, a izdaja je najteži grijeh. Podsjeća da je Dante izdajnike smjestio u **deveti krug pakla**. Sumnju naziva **najjačim đavoljim oružjem** kojim se razara Božje djelo.

Njezino djelovanje prikazuje kroz nekoliko primjera:

- svećeniku đavao šapće: „Zar misliš da ne smiješ leći sa ženom? Zar misliš da će se nešto dogoditi?“
- oženjenom muškarcu: „Zar misliš da će itko saznati? Vidi kako te želi“, i on to učini;
- onome tko je odlučio postiti do 19 sati: „Zar misliš da trebaš postiti? Tko ti je rekao da postiš?“

Zaključuje da se iza svake izdaje, bilo svećenika ili bračnog druga, krije isti uzrok: **„crv sumnje“** koji nagrize povjerenje u Boga. Zato Pavao poziva da se u svemu ima štit vjere, kao štit povjerenja u Boga i u ljude s kojima se nešto stvara.

magisterium.assessment: Povezivanje Pavlova „štita vjere” s otporom napasti ima biblijsku osnovu, a osuda bračne nevjere u skladu je s katoličkim naukom o bračnoj vjernosti. Ipak, odlomak pretjerano izjednačuje sumnju s đavoljim djelovanjem i izdaju proglašava najtežim grijehom bez potrebnih razlikovanja.
concerns: Nije svaka sumnja ili pitanje đavolje; sumnja može biti napast, ali i iskrena teškoća, razborito propitivanje ili poticaj da se istina bolje upozna. Odlomak može neopravdano obeshrabriti pitanja i prosuđivanje.
Tvrdnja da sumnja rađa izdaju i da se iza svake izdaje krije isti uzrok previše je općenita: grijeh uključuje slobodne odluke, a sumnja sama po sebi nije izdaja.

Izjava da je izdaja najteži grijeh nije predstavljena kao nauk Crkve; Danteovo smještanje izdajnika u deveti krug pripada književnoj pjesničkoj strukturi, a ne mjerodavnom nauku o težini svih grijeha.

Pavlov štit vjere odnosi se na pouzdanje i vjernost Bogu; povjerenje među ljudima može biti važno, ali nije istovjetno teologalnoj vjeri niti znači da se ljudsko ponašanje ne smije razborito prosuđivati.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao doista poziva vjernike da uzmu „štit vjere” kako bi ugasili ognjene strijele Zloga, pa je primjena slike na napast i povjerenje u Boga prikladna. Katoličko razumijevanje ipak razlikuje napast od pristanka na grijeh: moralna odgovornost vezana je uz slobodan čin, a bračna nevjera osuđuje se kao povreda bračne vjernosti, ne zato što je svaka sumnja već izdaja.

magisterium.assessment_en: Connecting Paul's "shield of faith" with resisting temptation has a biblical basis, and the condemnation of marital infidelity is in accordance with Catholic teaching on marital fidelity. Nevertheless, the passage excessively equates doubt with diabolical action and declares betrayal to be the gravest sin without the necessary distinctions.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul indeed calls believers to take "the shield of faith" to extinguish the flaming darts of the Evil One, so the application of the image to temptation and trust in God is appropriate. The Catholic understanding nevertheless distinguishes temptation from consent to sin: moral responsibility is tied to a free act, and marital infidelity is condemned as a violation of marital fidelity, not because every doubt is already betrayal.
concerns_en: Not every doubt or question is diabolical; doubt can be a temptation, but also a sincere difficulty, prudent questioning, or an impetus to know the truth better. The passage may unjustifiably discourage questions and evaluation.
The claim that doubt gives birth to betrayal and that behind every betrayal hides the same cause is too generalized: sin involves free decisions, and doubt in itself is not betrayal.

The statement that betrayal is the gravest sin is not presented as Church teaching; Dante's placement of traitors in the ninth circle belongs to a literary poetic structure, and not to authoritative teaching on the gravity of all sins.

Paul's shield of faith refers to trust and fidelity to God; trust among people may be important, but it is not identical to theological faith nor does it mean that human behavior must not be prudently evaluated.

sections.subtitle_en: Doubt as the devil's strongest weapon giving birth to betrayal
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about doubt as the source of betrayal and mentions Dante's ninth circle of hell
sections.content_en:
The devil's **flaming darts**, the host explains, are aimed precisely at sowing doubt. The questions pile up: "Did God really say?", "If you are the Son of God", "Did you really join that community? Do you know what they say about them?" As soon as someone speaks like that, Grebenar says, that comes from the devil.

Doubt, he continues, **gives birth to betrayal**, and betrayal is the gravest sin. He recalls that Dante placed traitors in the **ninth circle of hell**. He calls doubt the **devil's strongest weapon** with which God's work is destroyed.

He displays its action through several examples:

- to a priest the devil whispers: "Do you think you aren't allowed to lie with a woman? Do you think anything will happen?"
- to a married man: "Do you think anyone will find out? Look at how she wants you," and he does it;
- to someone who decided to fast until 7 PM: "Do you think you need to fast? Who told you to fast?"

He concludes that behind every betrayal, whether of a priest or a spouse, hides the same cause: the **"worm of doubt"** that eats away at trust in God. That is why Paul calls to take up in all things the shield of faith, as a shield of trust in God and in the people with whom something is being created.
keywords_en: flaming darts of the evil one

sections.subtitle: Kaciga spasenja: misao na grob i posljednji sud
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači kacigu spasenja kao podređivanje razuma srcu
sections.content:
**Kaciga spasenja** ide na glavu, pa je voditelj povezuje s razumom (*racio*). Uzeti kacigu spasenja znači **podrediti razum srcu**.

Budući da je razum „od tijela i krvi“, Grebenar poziva da u umu uvijek bude prisutna misao **da će se taj um, taj mozak i ta glava jednog dana raspasti u grobu**. Uz to treba imati na umu da na ovom svijetu ne vrijedi ništa što nije učinjeno u ljubavi i u vršenju volje Božje. „Neka ti se ureže u pamet da ćeš umrijeti, da te čeka posljednji sud“, poručuje.

Takva svijest, prema voditelju, mijenja način razmišljanja i odnose prema drugima, te **zatomljuje ego**. Čovjek tada lakše prihvaća druge sa svim njihovim slabostima, „takvi su kakvi su“.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen s kršćanskim pozivom na nadu u spasenje, svijest o odgovornosti pred Bogom, ljubav prema bližnjemu i poniznost; Efežanima 6,17 doista govori o „kacigi spasenja“. Ipak, poistovjećivanje kacige s podređivanjem razuma srcu nije izravno značenje Pavlove slike, a može biti nejasno ako zvuči kao umanjivanje razuma ili kao prihvaćanje tuđih slabosti bez razlikovanja između osobe i grijeha.
concerns: U Efežanima 6 kaciga je dio Božje opreme za duhovnu borbu i označava spasenje; tekst ne tumači izričito kacigu kao podređivanje razuma srcu. Takvu poveznicu zato treba predstaviti kao duhovnu primjenu, a ne kao doslovno Pavlovo tumačenje.

Izraz „prihvaća druge […] takvi su kakvi su“ može značiti strpljivo prihvaćanje ljudi, što je dobro, ali ne bi smio značiti odobravanje grijeha, odustajanje od istine ili zanemarivanje bratske opomene.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavlova slika kacige pripada cjelini duhovne opreme: kršćanin se oslanja na Božju snagu, vjeru i spasenje te ostaje postojan u duhovnoj borbi. Kršćanska vjera ne traži gašenje razuma: crkveni tekst o Pascalu naglašava da vjera nije protivna razumu, nego ga nadilazi, a istine vjere srce prima i razum ih može prepoznati i objašnjavati. Razmatranje smrti i suda može pomoći poniznosti i obraćenju, ali njegov plod treba biti ljubav koja strpljivo prihvaća osobu, a istodobno ostaje vjerna istini i dobru.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned with the Christian call to hope in salvation, awareness of responsibility before God, charity toward neighbor, and humility; Ephesians 6:17 indeed speaks of the "helmet of salvation." Nevertheless, equating the helmet with subordinating reason to the heart is not the direct meaning of Paul's image, and can be unclear if it sounds like diminishing reason or accepting others' weaknesses without distinguishing between the person and the sin.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul's image of the helmet belongs to the totality of spiritual armor: the Christian relies on God's strength, faith, and salvation, and remains steadfast in spiritual warfare. The Christian faith does not demand the extinguishing of reason: the Church text on Pascal emphasizes that faith is not contrary to reason, but transcends it, and the truths of faith are received by the heart while reason can recognize and explain them. Contemplation of death and judgment can aid humility and conversion, but its fruit should be charity that patiently accepts the person while remaining faithful to truth and goodness.
concerns_en: In Ephesians 6, the helmet is part of God's armor for spiritual warfare and signifies salvation; the text does not explicitly interpret the helmet as subordinating reason to the heart. Such a connection should therefore be presented as a spiritual application, and not as Paul's literal interpretation.
The expression "accepts others [...] as they are" can mean patient acceptance of people, which is good, but it should not mean approving sin, abandoning truth, or neglecting fraternal correction.

sections.subtitle_en: Helmet of salvation: thought of the grave and the final judgment
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets the helmet of salvation as subordinating reason to the heart
sections.content_en:
The **helmet of salvation** goes on the head, so the host connects it with reason (*ratio*). Taking the helmet of salvation means **subordinating reason to the heart**.

Since reason is "of flesh and blood," Grebenar calls for the thought to always be present in the mind **that that mind, that brain, and that head will one day decompose in the grave**. Along with that, one should keep in mind that in this world nothing is of worth that was not done in love and in doing the will of God. "Let it be engraved in your mind that you will die, that the final judgment awaits you," he conveys.

Such an awareness, according to the host, changes the way of thinking and relationships toward others, and **subdues the ego**. A person then more easily accepts others with all their weaknesses, "they are as they are."

sections.subtitle: Mač duha i proroštvo: zašto nijedna emisija nije uklonjena
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava zašto je sve emisije i podcaste ostavio javno dostupnima na YouTubeu
sections.content:
**Mač duha** je, prema Pavlu, riječ Božja. Voditelj ga povezuje s **proroštvom**, s otvorenošću da čovjek govori ono što mu dolazi u molitvi. Priznaje da i sam često kaže „dobih u molitvi“, ali ne tvrdi da je to stopostotno tako, jer je **„nesavršeno naše prorokovanje“**.

Iznosi i kriterij razlučivanja: tko tvrdi da je nešto sigurno dobio od Boga, time pokazuje da nije od Boga. Onaj tko uistinu primi riječ od Gospodina reći će: „Vjerujem da sam dobio. Neka se ovo propita, neka se razluči je li od Gospodina.“ Duh Sveti, ističe Grebenar, nema problem s time da ga se propituje.

Na tome temelji i odluku da sve emisije i podcaste, od prvog do posljednjeg, ostavi na **YouTubeu**. Nijednu nije uklonio i ni zbog jedne se ne stidi. Kad bi nešto što je rekao bilo protivno Gospodinu, objašnjava, skrivao bi emisije, jednu pa petu pa sedmu. Ovako sve ostaje dostupno da se propita. Naglašava da to govori otvoreno, svjestan svega što je izgovorio.

Objašnjava i dubinu proročke riječi. Ljudi govore ono što je „istinito“, a istinu govori Duh Sveti kroz ljude. Takva riječ dolazi iz vječnosti, pa nije ograničena vremenom: **djeluje na prošlost, sadašnjost i budućnost**, kao što je i Isusova žrtva na križu za sva vremena. Riječ Božja tako „reže“: u prošlosti lomi prokletstvo i oslobađa čovjeka i njegove rođake, u budućnosti blagoslivlja potomstvo da ostane u vjeri, a u sadašnjosti rješava probleme i donosi mir.

magisterium.assessment: Ispravno je povezati mač Duha s Božjom riječju i naglasiti potrebu razlučivanja, jer Pavao tako tumači mač Duha, a privatni proročki poticaji mogu biti nesavršeni ili pogrešno pripisani Bogu. Ipak, tvrdnje da sigurnost u božansko podrijetlo sama po sebi dokazuje da poruka nije od Boga te da proročka riječ razrješava prokletstva iz prošlosti i unaprijed blagoslivlja potomstvo iznose se previše kategorično i pripisuju takvim riječima učinke koje navedeni izvori ne potvrđuju.
concerns: Zaključak da osoba koja tvrdi da je nešto sigurno primila od Boga time dokazuje da poruka nije od Boga nije valjan kriterij razlučivanja; izvori razlikuju savršeno i nesavršeno proroštvo, pri čemu primatelj nesavršenog poticaja možda ne zna jasno dolazi li on od Boga ili iz vlastitog duha.

To što voditelj ostavlja sve emisije na YouTubeu i ne stidi se izgovorenoga ne dokazuje da su njegove tvrdnje istinite ni da su od Boga; sadržaj treba prosuđivati prema vjeri i razumu, a ne prema tome je li javno dostupan.

Tvrdnja da proročka riječ djeluje na prošlost, sadašnjost i budućnost, lomi prokletstva za rođake i blagoslivlja potomstvo nadilazi ono što potkrepljuju navedeni izvori. Kristovo dovršeno objavljenje u Sinu ne znači da je svaki ljudski proročki iskaz božanski učinkovit ili da može mijenjati prošle događaje.
magisterium.enrichment: Pavao izričito naziva mačem Duha Božju riječ, u sklopu opreme koja uključuje istinu, pravednost, vjeru i ustrajnu molitvu; zato se slika prvenstveno odnosi na vjernost evanđelju i duhovnu borbu, a ne na jamstvo da je svaki osobni poticaj nadahnut. Crkva uči da Bog može objaviti budućnost, ali kršćanin se treba pouzdati u Providnost, a ne tražiti sigurnost u privatnim objavama.
