magisterium.assessment_en: It is correct to connect the sword of the Spirit with the Word of God and emphasize the need for discernment, because Paul so interprets the sword of the Spirit, and private prophetic promptings can be imperfect or mistakenly attributed to God. Nevertheless, the claims that certainty of divine origin in itself proves the message is not from God, and that a prophetic word dissolves curses from the past and blesses descendants in advance, are asserted too categorically and attribute to such words effects that the cited sources do not confirm.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Paul explicitly calls the sword of the Spirit the Word of God, as part of armor that includes truth, righteousness, faith, and persevering prayer; therefore, the image primarily refers to fidelity to the Gospel and spiritual warfare, rather than to a guarantee that every personal prompting is inspired. The Church teaches that God can reveal the future, but the Christian should trust in Providence, and not seek certainty in private revelations.
concerns_en: The conclusion that a person who claims to have received something with certainty from God thereby proves that the message is not from God is not a valid criterion of discernment; sources distinguish perfect and imperfect prophecy, where the recipient of an imperfect prompting might not clearly know whether it comes from God or from their own spirit.

The fact that the host leaves all episodes on YouTube and is not ashamed of what was spoken does not prove that his claims are true or that they are from God; content should be judged according to faith and reason, and not according to whether it is publicly available.

The claim that a prophetic word acts upon the past, present, and future, breaks curses for relatives, and blesses posterity exceeds what is substantiated by the cited sources. Christ's definitive revelation in the Son does not mean that every human prophetic utterance is divinely effective or that it can alter past events.

sections.subtitle_en: Sword of the Spirit and prophecy: why not a single broadcast was removed
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host explains why he left all broadcasts and podcasts publicly available on YouTube
sections.content_en:
The **sword of the Spirit** is, according to Paul, the word of God. The host connects it with **prophecy**, with openness for a person to speak what comes to him in prayer. He admits that he himself often says "I received in prayer," but does not claim that it is a hundred percent so, because **"our prophesying is imperfect"**.

He also presents a criterion of discernment: whoever claims that he has certainly received something from God thereby shows that he is not from God. The one who truly receives a word from the Lord will say: "I believe I received it. Let this be tested, let it be discerned whether it is from the Lord." The Holy Spirit, Grebenar points out, has no problem with being tested.

On that he also bases the decision to leave all broadcasts and podcasts, from the first to the last, on **YouTube**. He has not removed a single one and is not ashamed because of any of them. If anything he said were contrary to the Lord, he explains, he would hide broadcasts, one then a fifth then a seventh. This way everything remains available to be examined. He emphasizes that he speaks this openly, conscious of everything he has uttered.

He also explains the depth of the prophetic word. People speak what is "truthful," while the Holy Spirit speaks the truth through people. Such a word comes from eternity, so it is not limited by time: **it acts upon the past, the present, and the future**, just as Jesus' sacrifice on the cross is for all times. The word of God thus "cuts": in the past it breaks a curse and liberates a person and his relatives, in the future it blesses posterity to remain in faith, and in the present it resolves problems and brings peace.

sections.subtitle: Nezaštićena leđa: tko ti čuva leđa?
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj ističe da oprema Božja ne štiti leđa jer trebamo jedni druge
sections.content:
Završni Pavlov poziv na molitvu u duhu voditelj povezuje s jednim zanimljivim zapažanjem: **u cijeloj opremi Božjoj jedan dio tijela ostaje nezaštićen, a to su leđa**. Razlog vidi upravo u štitu vjere: ljudi moraju imati povjerenja jedni u druge.

Tu ponovno spominje izdaju u braku. Kad muž prevari ženu ili žena muža, raskida se bračni odnos, pa Isus kaže da se žena ne smije otpustiti osim zbog preljuba. Grebenar ponavlja da **nema težeg grijeha od izdaje**. Na isti način i **okultizam** naziva izdajom Boga, „preljubom sa samim Sotonom protiv Boga“, kao što je tjelesni preljub izdaja bračnog druga. Te teške grijehe, kaže, Bog koristi kao slike kako bi ljudi razumjeli o čemu je riječ.

Poruka je jasna: **„Moraš znati tko ti leđa čuva.“** Povjerenje kao štit vjere izgrađuje se kroz vrijeme i odnos, a Bog dopušta i da se njegovo djelo iskuša.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno naglašava ozbiljnost bračne nevjere i koristi biblijski utemeljenu sliku duhovne nevjere za idolopoklonstvo i okultizam. Međutim, tvrdnja da su leđa namjerno nezaštićena i da štit vjere znači međusobno povjerenje nije ono što Ef 6 izričito kaže, a proglašavanje izdaje „najvećim grijehom“ neopravdano postavlja apsolutnu ljestvicu grijeha.
concerns: Ef 6 prikazuje opremu Božju kao sredstva za odupiranje zlu: Pavao navodi istinu, pravednost, evanđelje mira, vjeru, spasenje i Božju riječ te poziva na ustrajnu molitvu. Ne kaže da su leđa nezaštićena niti da je štit vjere povjerenje u druge ljude; takva primjena može biti homiletska metafora, ali ne bi je trebalo predstavljati kao značenje teksta.

Bračna nevjera teško ranjava supružnika i protivi se vjernosti bračnom savezu, ali dostupni izvori ne utemeljuju tvrdnju da nema težeg grijeha od izdaje. Bolje je osuditi nevjeru jasno, a da se ne rangiraju svi grijesi absoluuttisesti.

Okultizam se može kuvati kao duhovna nevjera Bogu, ali izraz „preljub sa samim Sotonom“ treba jasno označiti kao slikoviti izraz, ne kao doslovan opis. Biblijski prikaz proročke slike nevjere odnosi se na idolopoklonstvo i izdaju saveza s Gospodinom.

Tvrdnja da Isus dopušta otpustiti ženu samo zbog preljuba pojednostavljuje evanđeoski nauk o braku i može zvučati kao da preljub automatski razrješuje ženidbeni vez. Katolički nauk ističe nerazrješivost valjanog, sklopljenog i izvršenog ženidbenog veza, uz razlikovanje od mogućnosti rastave supružnika u određenim okolnostima.
magisterium.enrichment: U Ef 6 „štit vjere“ pripada Pavlovoj slici duhovne borbe protiv zla, a cjelina naglašava stajanje čvrsto u Gospodinu, istini, pravednosti, evanđelju i molitvi. Vjera može nadahnjivati povjerenje i solidarnost među kršćanima, ali ta je primjena pastoralna posljedica, a ne izravno značenje štita u odlomku. Pismo doista koristi sliku bračne nevjere za nevjernost naroda Bogu, no uz osudu nevjernosti naviješta i Božji poziv na povratak i milosrđe.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly emphasizes the seriousness of marital infidelity and uses the biblically grounded image of spiritual infidelity for idolatry and the occult. However, the claim that the back is intentionally unprotected and that the shield of faith means mutual trust is not what Eph 6 explicitly states, and declaring betrayal to be the "greatest sin" unjustifiably establishes an absolute ranking of sins.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Eph 6 the "shield of faith" belongs to Paul's imagery of spiritual warfare against evil, and the whole emphasizes standing firm in the Lord, truth, righteousness, the Gospel, and prayer. Faith can inspire trust and solidarity among Christians, but that application is a pastoral consequence, not the direct meaning of the shield in the passage. Scripture indeed uses the image of marital infidelity for the infidelity of the people to God, yet alongside the condemnation of infidelity it also proclaims God's call to return and mercy.
concerns_en: Eph 6 depicts the armor of God as means to resist evil: Paul lists truth, righteousness, the gospel of peace, faith, salvation, and the Word of God, and calls for persevering prayer. He does not say that the back is unprotected or that the shield of faith is trust in other people; such an application may be a homiletic metaphor, but should not be presented as the meaning of the text.

Marital infidelity severely wounds the spouse and is contrary to fidelity to the marital covenant, but available sources do not substantiate the claim that there is no sin graver than betrayal. It is better to condemn infidelity clearly without ranking all sins absolutely.

Occultism can be viewed as spiritual infidelity to God, but the expression "adultery with Satan himself" should be clearly marked as figurative language, not as a literal description. The biblical presentation of prophetic imagery of infidelity refers to idolatry and betrayal of the covenant with the Lord.

The claim that Jesus allows divorcing a wife only because of adultery oversimplifies the Gospel teaching on marriage and can sound as though adultery automatically dissolves the marital bond. Catholic teaching emphasizes the indissolubility of a valid, ratified, and consummated marriage bond, distinguishing it from the possibility of separation of spouses under certain circumstances.

sections.subtitle_en: Unprotected back: who watches your back?
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host points out that the armor of God does not protect the back because we need one another
sections.content_en:
Paul's concluding call to pray in the spirit the host connects with an interesting observation: **in the whole armor of God, one part of the body remains unprotected, and that is the back**. He sees the reason precisely in the shield of faith: people must have trust in one another.

Here he mentions again betrayal in marriage. When a husband cheats on his wife or a wife on her husband, the marital relationship is broken, so Jesus says that a wife must not be dismissed except for unchastity. Grebenar repeats that **there is no graver sin than betrayal**. In the same way, he calls **occultism** a betrayal of God, "adultery with Satan himself against God," just as physical adultery is betrayal of a spouse. Those grave sins, he says, God uses as images so that people might understand what it is about.

The message is clear: **"You must know who watches your back."** Trust as the shield of faith is built through time and relationship, and God allows His work to be tested as well.

sections.subtitle: Kušnja u pustinji i pad anđela: povjerenje kao temelj svakog djela
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači Isusovu kušnju u pustinji u kojoj đavao citira Sveto pismo
sections.content:
Kao primjer iskušavanja Božjeg djela voditelj navodi **Isusovu kušnju u pustinji**. Bog Otac dopustio je da ga đavao napadne, a Isus ga je otjerao štitom vjere. Grebenar upozorava na zanimljiv detalj: đavao je nakon posijane sumnje uzeo i sam „mač duha“, odnosno **citirao Sveto pismo**: „Zapovjedit će anđelima svojim da te pridrže da se ne spotakneš.“ Isus mu je odgovorio istim oružjem: „Također je pisano: Ne iskušavaj Gospodina Boga svojega.“ To voditelj tumači kao poruku: ne testiraj vjeru i povjerenje u Boga.

Isti obrazac pronalazi i u **padu anđela**. Kerubin koji je pao, a u nebu se još nije zvao đavao, iskušavao je i narušio odnos s Bogom. Bog je u njega imao bezgranično povjerenje, a on u Boga nije, pa je izbačen.

Zaključak je da se **ništa ne može graditi bez povjerenja**. Povjerenje, a zatim odgovornost, preduvjeti su da se s drugim ljudima napravi nešto veliko. Voditelj iznosi i vlastiti pristup: kad osjeti da netko od bližnjih sumnja u njega, najprije ispituje je li sam negdje pogriješio. Ako razluči da nije, nego da osoba sumnja iz drugih razloga, primjerice jer od njega nešto traži ili joj je potreban radi vlastitog probitka, odmah se distancira i prepušta joj da to „rješava s Gospodinom“.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje Isusove kušnje uglavnom je usklađeno: đavao doista citira Pismo, ali ga izvrće, a Isus odgovara ispravnom primjenom Božje riječi i odbija iskušavati Boga. Slabije je utemeljeno pojednostavljeno objašnjenje pada anđela kao posljedice manjka povjerenja u Boga te zaključak da je neposredno distanciranje uvijek prikladan odgovor na tuđu sumnju.
concerns: Tvrdnja da je Bog imao „bezgranično povjerenje” u palog kerubina, a ovaj nije uzvratio povjerenjem pa je zato izbačen, prikazuje pad anđela kao ljudski odnos povjerenja i ne daje dovoljno teološkog objašnjenja slobodnog odbacivanja Boga. Označavanje palog anđela kao kerubina također nije potkrijepljeno navedenim biblijskim opisom.
„Štit vjere” prikladna je poveznica s Ef 6, ali evanđeoski tekst kušnje naglašava da Isus pobjeđuje odgovorom iz Pisma; ne treba miješati tu teološku sliku s izričitim detaljem evanđeoskog prikaza.

Osobni stav da se treba odmah distancirati kad se procijeni da netko sumnja iz sebičnih razloga može biti razborita granica u pojedinim slučajevima, ali kao opće pravilo može potaknuti preuranjeno pripisivanje motiva i izostanak dijaloga ili pomirenja.
magisterium.enrichment: Katoličko tumačenje kušnje ističe da Isus pobjeđuje ostajući poslušan Ocu: đavao se služi riječima Pisma, ali ih Isus pravilno primjenjuje i odbacuje zahtjev da Boga podvrgne kušnji. Evanđeoska kušnja zato nije samo primjer „povjerenja” općenito, nego pokazuje vjernost Sina Ocu i pobjedu nad napastima koje su povezane s kušnjama Izraela i Adama. U odnosima među ljudima povjerenje je važno, ali kršćanska razboritost uključuje i samopreispitivanje, pravedno razlučivanje te nastojanje oko istine i mira, bez brzog proglašavanja tuđih motiva.

magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation of Jesus' temptation is mainly aligned: the devil indeed quotes Scripture, but twists it, and Jesus responds with the correct application of the Word of God and refuses to put God to the test. Less well-founded is the simplified explanation of the fall of the angels as a consequence of a lack of trust in God and the conclusion that immediate distancing is always an appropriate response to another's doubt.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Catholic interpretation of the temptation emphasizes that Jesus conquers by remaining obedient to the Father: the devil uses the words of Scripture, but Jesus correctly applies them and rejects the demand to put God to the test. The Gospel temptation is therefore not merely an example of "trust" in general, but demonstrates the Son's fidelity to the Father and victory over temptations linked to the testings of Israel and Adam. In human relationships trust is important, but Christian prudence also includes self-examination, fair discernment, and striving for truth and peace, without hastily labeling others' motives.
concerns_en: The claim that God had "boundless trust" in the fallen cherub, and that he did not return trust and was therefore cast out, depicts the fall of the angels as a human relationship of trust and does not provide sufficient theological explanation of the free rejection of God. Labeling the fallen angel as a cherub is likewise not supported by the cited biblical description.

The "shield of faith" is an appropriate link to Eph 6, but the Gospel text of the temptation emphasizes that Jesus conquers with an answer from Scripture; one should not confuse that theological image with an explicit detail of the Gospel account.

The personal stance that one should immediately distance oneself when it is evaluated that someone doubts for selfish reasons can be a prudent boundary in particular cases, but as a general rule it can encourage premature attribution of motives and the absence of dialogue or reconciliation.

sections.subtitle_en: Temptation in the desert and the fall of the angels: trust as the foundation of every deed
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets Jesus' temptation in the desert in which the devil quotes Sacred Scripture
sections.content_en:
As an example of testing God's work, the host cites **Jesus' temptation in the desert**. God the Father permitted the devil to attack him, and Jesus drove him away with the shield of faith. Grebenar warns of an interesting detail: after sowing doubt, the devil himself took up the "sword of the spirit," that is, **quoted Sacred Scripture**: "He will command his angels concerning you to guard you so that you do not strike your foot against a stone." Jesus answered him with the same weapon: "It is also written: Do not put the Lord your God to the test." The host interprets this as the message: do not test faith and trust in God.

He finds the same pattern in the **fall of the angels**. The cherub who fell, and in heaven was not yet called the devil, tested and damaged the relationship with God. God had boundless trust in him, and he did not have it in God, so he was cast out.

The conclusion is that **nothing can be built without trust**. Trust, and then responsibility, are prerequisites for doing something great with other people. The host also presents his own approach: when he feels that someone close to him doubts him, he first examines whether he made a mistake somewhere himself. If he discerns that he did not, but that the person doubts for other reasons, for example because they seek something from him or need him for their own advancement, he immediately distances himself and leaves it to them to "resolve it with the Lord."

sections.subtitle: „Blagoslovljen Gospodin, hridina moja“: ispit povjerenja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj čita psalam i poziva na ispit povjerenja prema Bogu
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim čita psalam dana: „Blagoslovljen Gospodin, hridina moja, ruke mi uči boju, a prste ratu“. Psalmist u njemu Boga naziva ljubavlju, tvrđavom, zaštitom, izbaviteljem i štitom te mu obećava pjesmu novu na harfi od deset žica.

U tim riječima Grebenar prepoznaje **duboko povjerenje** i poziva slušatelje da toga dana ispitaju vlastito povjerenje prema Bogu. Oni koji su u zajednici trebaju ispitati i povjerenje prema onima koji su Božji.

Pritom pravi jasnu razliku. Prema **lažnoj braći**, kojih ima i u molitvenim zajednicama i u firmama, ne može se imati povjerenja, pa prema njima treba biti „mudar kao zmija“. Prema pravoj, otvorenoj braći Isus poziva na jednostavnost goluba u komunikaciji. Na prvom mjestu ipak ostaje povjerenje prema Bogu, prema zapovijedi: ljubi Boga svim srcem, a onda bližnjega kao sebe samoga.

magisterium.assessment: Naglasak na pouzdanju u Boga i povezivanje Isusovih riječi o mudrosti zmije i nevinosti goluba uglavnom su u skladu s katoličkim tumačenjem Mt 10,16. Ipak, tvrdnja da se lažnoj braći ne može vjerovati izrečena je preširoko i može poticati sumnjičavost ako se ne poveže s razboritim prosuđivanjem, nevinošću i ljubavlju prema bližnjemu.
concerns: Mt 10,16 poziva istodobno na oprez i na nevinost, a ne na opću nepovjerljivost ili uzvraćanje prijevarom; tumačenje naglašava razboritost i čestitost u postupanju.

Označavanje pojedinaca kao lažne braće bez objašnjenja kako se takva procjena razborito donosi može dovesti do neopravdanog osuđivanja ili nepovjerenja. Odlomak djelomično ublažava tu opasnost razlikujući mudrost od jednostavnosti, ali bi trebao jasnije reći da oprez ne isključuje kršćansku ljubav.
magisterium.enrichment: U Mt 10,16 Isus šalje učenike u opasno okruženje te traži da zajedno čuvaju razboritost zmije i nevinost goluba: kršćanska razboritost prepoznaje opasnost, dok nevinost isključuje prijevaru i osvetoljubivost. Zato je moguće biti oprezan u odnosima, a ipak prema svima postupati s poštovanjem i bez brzog osuđivanja; papinska kateheza tu kršćansku vrlinu opisuje kao spoj jednostavnosti i pronicavosti.

magisterium.assessment_en: The emphasis on trust in God and linking Jesus' words about the wisdom of serpents and the innocence of doves are mainly in accordance with the Catholic interpretation of Mt 10:16. Nevertheless, the claim that false brethren cannot be trusted is stated too broadly and can foster suspicion if not linked with prudent judgment, innocence, and love of neighbor.
magisterium.enrichment_en: In Mt 10:16 Jesus sends disciples into a dangerous environment and asks that they preserve together the prudence of serpents and the innocence of doves: Christian prudence recognizes danger, while innocence excludes deceit and vindictiveness. Therefore, it is possible to be cautious in relationships, yet treat everyone with respect and without hasty condemnation; papal catechesis describes this Christian virtue as a union of simplicity and discernment.
concerns_en: Mt 10:16 calls simultaneously for caution and innocence, not for general mistrust or repaying with deceit; the interpretation emphasizes prudence and uprightness in conduct.

Labeling individuals as false brethren without explaining how such an evaluation is prudently made can lead to unjustified condemnation or mistrust. The passage partially mitigates that danger by distinguishing wisdom from simplicity, but should state more clearly that caution does not exclude Christian charity.

sections.subtitle_en: "Blessed be the Lord, my rock": an examination of trust
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reads the psalm and calls for an examination of trust toward God
sections.content_en:
The host then reads the psalm of the day: "Blessed be the Lord, my rock, who trains my hands for war, and my fingers for battle." In it, the psalmist calls God his love, fortress, protection, deliverer, and shield, and promises Him a new song on a ten-stringed harp.

In those words, Grebenar recognizes **deep trust** and calls the listeners to examine on that day their own trust toward God. Those who are in a community should also examine trust toward those who belong to God.

In doing so, he makes a clear distinction. Toward **false brothers**, of whom there are both in prayer communities and in companies, one cannot have trust, so toward them one must be "wise as serpents." Toward true, open brothers, Jesus calls for the simplicity of doves in communication. In first place nevertheless remains trust toward God, according to the commandment: love God with all your heart, and then your neighbor as yourself.

sections.subtitle: „Idite i kažite toj lisici“: Isus bez straha pred Herodom
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači kako Isus bez straha naziva Heroda lisicom
sections.content:
Slijedi evanđelje dana. Farizeji pristupaju Isusu i upozoravaju ga da ode jer ga **Herod** hoće ubiti. Isus odgovara: „Idite i kažite toj lisici: evo, izgonim đavle i liječim danas i sutra, a treći dan dovršujem“, dodajući da mora nastaviti put jer „ne priliči da prorok pogine izvan Jeruzalema“.

Voditelj pita je li se Isus uplašio. Odgovor je niječan: Isus odgovara izravno riječju Božjom, **ne boji se ni farizeja ni Heroda**, a Heroda još naziva lisicom. Riječima „izgonim đavle i liječim“ Isus zapravo kaže da vrši volju Božju i čini točno ono što Bog želi.

Izraz „danas i sutra, a treći dan dovršujem“ Grebenar tumači kao **židovsku poslovicu** koja znači „prezauzet sam“. Smisao Isusove poruke Herodu prenosi ovako: „Nemam vremena za tebe. Nisi bitan, nisi Bog. Ne bojim te se. Vršim volju Božju.“ Riječi „moram nastaviti put“ pokazuju da je Bog Otac Isusu dao zapovijed što mora činiti.

magisterium.assessment: Tumačenje uglavnom vjerno prenosi Lukin prikaz Isusove odlučnosti: Herodova prijetnja ne zaustavlja njegovo poslanje, a Isus svjesno ide prema dovršenju djela i smrti u Jeruzalemu. Ipak, tvrdnju da je „danas i sutra, a treći dan“ židovska poslovica koja znači „prezauzet sam“ te parafrazu „nisi bitan“ treba ublažiti jer priloženi komentari ne potvrđuju takvo značenje.
concerns: U priloženim komentarima „danas i sutra“ tumači se kao razdoblje tijekom kojega Isus nastavlja djelovati, a niz dana može upućivati i na blizinu dovršenja; nije potvrđeno da je riječ o poslovici sa značenjem „prezauzet sam“.

„Nisi bitan“ zvuči kao slobodna, pojačana parafraza, a ne kao izričit sadržaj evanđeoskog teksta. Sigurnije je naglasiti da Herod nema vlast zaustaviti Isusovo poslanje te da Isus samovoljno prihvaća put prema Jeruzalemu.
magisterium.enrichment: Naziv „lisica“ u katoličkim komentarima označuje Herodovu lukavost i prijetvornost, a Isusov odgovor pokazuje da neće napustiti djelo koje vrši. Riječi „mora“ i „dovršujem“ ne treba shvatiti kao prisilu koja ukida Isusovu slobodu: komentari ističu da Isus ide prema svojoj muci vlastitom voljom, u skladu s poslanjem koje mu je povjereno. Spominjanje Jeruzalema zato nije samo geografska napomena, nego nagovještaj da će se Isusovo proročko poslanje dovršiti njegovom smrću ondje.
magisterium.assessment_en: The interpretation mainly faithfully conveys Luke's depiction of Jesus' determination: Herod's threat does not stop his mission, and Jesus consciously goes toward the completion of his work and death in Jerusalem. Still, the claim that "today and tomorrow, and the third day" is a Jewish proverb meaning "I am too busy" and the paraphrase "you are not important" should be softened because the attached commentaries do not confirm such a meaning.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The designation "fox" in Catholic commentaries signifies Herod's cunning and craftiness, and Jesus' response shows that he will not abandon the work he is carrying out. The words "must" and "finish" should not be understood as compulsion that abolishes Jesus' freedom: commentaries emphasize that Jesus goes toward his Passion of his own will, in accordance with the mission entrusted to him. The mention of Jerusalem is therefore not merely a geographical note, but an intimation that Jesus' prophetic mission will be completed by his death there.
concerns_en: In the attached commentaries "today and tomorrow" is interpreted as the period during which Jesus continues to act, and the sequence of days can also point to the nearness of completion; it is not confirmed that this is a proverb with the meaning "I am too busy."

"You are not important" sounds like a free, intensified paraphrase, and not like the explicit content of the Gospel text. It is safer to emphasize that Herod has no power to stop Jesus' mission and that Jesus willingly embraces the path toward Jerusalem.

sections.subtitle_en: "Go and tell that fox": Jesus without fear before Herod
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host interprets how Jesus without fear calls Herod a fox
sections.content_en:
The gospel of the day follows. The Pharisees approach Jesus and warn him to leave because **Herod** wants to kill him. Jesus answers: "Go and tell that fox: Behold, I cast out demons and perform cures today and tomorrow, and the third day I finish," adding that he must continue his journey because "it is impossible that a prophet should perish outside of Jerusalem."

The host asks whether Jesus was afraid. The answer is negative: Jesus answers directly with the word of God, **fearing neither the Pharisees nor Herod**, and even calls Herod a fox. With the words "I cast out demons and perform cures" Jesus is actually saying that he does the will of God and does exactly what God desires.

The expression "today and tomorrow, and the third day I finish" Grebenar interprets as a **Jewish proverb** that means "I am too busy." He conveys the meaning of Jesus' message to Herod like this: "I have no time for you. You are not important, you are not God. I am not afraid of you. I do the will of God." The words "I must continue my journey" show that God the Father gave Jesus a commandment about what he must do.

sections.subtitle: Poslušnost u obitelji, kilometri promocija i spremnost na žrtvu
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o putovanjima na promocije i povratcima kući obitelji
sections.content:
Isusovu poslušnost Ocu voditelj povezuje s vlastitim iskustvom. Svojoj djeci, kaže, nešto kaže samo jednom i ne ponavlja, a ona slušaju. Odbacuje dojam da je prestrog i tvrdi da to znaju svi koji poznaju njegovu obitelj. Razlog je drugi: **Gospodin je njega „doveo u red“** tako da on posluša kad mu Bog nešto kaže jednom. Kad zna da je nešto Božje, ne zaustavlja se, nego po Isusovu uzoru „danas, sutra i prekosutra dovršava“.

Isti obrazac vidi i u svojoj službi. Ljudima koji se čude kako mu se da obilaziti promocije opisuje da odmah nakon snimanja podcasta sjeda u auto i odlazi u grad udaljen 150 do 200 kilometara, „zato što Isus tako čini“. Vraća se iz **Knina u Hercegovinu**, pa sutradan ponovno odlazi u **Drniš**. Na pitanje zašto se uopće vraća odgovara da je otac i da želi vidjeti ženu i djecu, iako bi mu bilo lakše ostati. Pritom zna da mora završiti ono što je Gospodin stavio pred njega.

Komentarima da ga „nešto goni“ suprotstavlja pitanje: što je goni Isusa? Odgovor nalazi u riječima „ne priliči da prorok pogine izvan Jeruzalema“. Iz toga izvodi poruku: tko želi vršiti volju Božju, mora biti spreman reći da ne priliči stradati ondje gdje Bog to nije odredio, ali i **biti spreman ići u smrt za Gospodina** ako je on tako odlučio.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak je uglavnom usklađen u isticanju poslušnosti Bogu, Kristova primjera i spremnosti na žrtvu, a povratak obitelji sam po sebi pokazuje da služenje ne znači zanemarivanje obiteljskih obveza. Ipak, primjena Isusove izjave o Jeruzalemu na opće pravilo da čovjek treba znati gdje mu je Bog odredio stradati nije dovoljno obrazložena i može zvučati kao pretjerano sigurno tumačenje Božje volje.
concerns: Isusove riječi o tome da prorok ne pogine izvan Jeruzalema odnose se na njegovu vlastitu misiju i put prema Jeruzalemu; iz njih se ne može bez dodatnog obrazloženja izvesti opće pravilo da pojedinac može znati gdje je Bog odredio da strada. U dostavljenom biblijskom izvatku potvrđeno je da Isusa upozoravaju na Herodovu prijetnju, ali nije naveden nastavak odlomka s izjavom o Jeruzalemu.

Tvrdnja da se djeca odazovu nakon jedne roditeljske upute može biti osobno svjedočanstvo, ali ne bi je trebalo shvatiti kao opravdanje za bezuvjetnu ili prestrogu roditeljsku vlast: Pavao istodobno poziva djecu na poslušnost „u Gospodinu“, a očevima nalaže da ne izazivaju djecu na srdžbu.
magisterium.enrichment: Kršćanska poslušnost Bogu ima prvenstvo pred svim ljudskim vezama, ali obiteljske dužnosti nisu zbog toga bezvrijedne: Isus je poslušnost Ocu živio i kroz podložnost Mariji i Josipu, dok se obiteljske veze relativiziraju samo kada bi priječile vjernost Božjem pozivu. Spremnost na mučeništvo može biti vjerno evanđelju, no razlikuje se od zaključka da je čovjeku unaprijed poznato mjesto ili način njegove smrti; naglasak odlomka iz Poslanice Efežanima jest ustrajati u vjeri, molitvi i naviještanju evanđelja.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage is mainly aligned in emphasizing obedience to God, Christ's example, and readiness for sacrifice, and returning to the family in itself shows that service does not mean neglecting family obligations. However, applying Jesus' statement about Jerusalem to a general rule that a person should know where God has destined them to suffer is not sufficiently explained and can sound like an overly confident interpretation of God's will.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Christian obedience to God takes precedence over all human ties, but family duties are not thereby worthless: Jesus lived obedience to the Father also through subjection to Mary and Joseph, while family ties are relativized only when they would hinder fidelity to God's call. Readiness for martyrdom can be faithful to the Gospel, yet differs from the conclusion that the place or manner of one's death is known to a person in advance; the emphasis of the passage from the Epistle to the Ephesians is to persevere in faith, prayer, and the proclamation of the Gospel.
concerns_en: Jesus' words that a prophet does not perish outside Jerusalem refer to his own mission and journey toward Jerusalem; from them one cannot, without additional explanation, derive a general rule that an individual can know where God has destined them to suffer. In the provided biblical excerpt it is confirmed that Jesus is warned about Herod's threat, but the continuation of the passage with the statement about Jerusalem is not cited.

The claim that children respond after a single parental instruction may be personal testimony, but should not be understood as justification for unconditional or overly strict parental authority: Paul simultaneously calls children to obedience "in the Lord," and commands fathers not to provoke their children to anger.

sections.subtitle_en: Obedience in the family, kilometers of promotions, and readiness for sacrifice
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host speaks about traveling to promotions and returning home to his family
sections.content_en:
The host connects Jesus' obedience to the Father with his own experience. To his children, he says, he says something only once and does not repeat it, and they obey. He rejects the impression that he is too strict and claims that everyone who knows his family knows this. The reason is different: **the Lord "brought him into order"** so that he obeys when God tells him something once. When he knows that something is of God, he does not stop, but following Jesus' example "today, tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow finishes."

He sees the same pattern in his ministry. To people who wonder how he can bear to travel around to book promotions, he describes that right after recording the podcast he gets into his car and leaves for a town 150 to 200 kilometers away, "because Jesus does so." He returns from **Knin to Hercegovina**, and then the next day leaves again for **Drniš**. To the question of why he returns at all, he answers that he is a father and wants to see his wife and children, although it would be easier for him to stay. At the same time, he knows that he must finish what the Lord has placed before him.

To comments that "something is driving him" he counters with the question: what drove Jesus? He finds the answer in the words "it is impossible that a prophet should perish outside of Jerusalem." From that he derives the message: whoever wishes to do the will of God must be ready to say that it is not fitting to perish where God did not designate it, but also **be ready to go to death for the Lord** if He has so decided.

sections.subtitle: Tužaljka nad Jeruzalemom i pogled na današnju Hrvatsku
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj povezuje Isusovu tužaljku nad Jeruzalemom s Hrvatskom i Međugorjem
sections.content:
Isusovu tešku riječ nad Jeruzalemom, koji ubija proroke i kamenuje one koji su mu poslani, voditelj tumači kao osudu grada kojemu je Bog slao glasnike. Uspoređuje je s pričom o **Joni**, kojega je Bog poslao u pogansku **Ninivu**. Ninivljani su se obratili, a Židovi vjernici nisu, što Grebenar naziva primjerom „lažne braće“.

Riječi „koliko li puta htjedoh skupiti djecu tvoju kao kvočka piliće pod krila i ne htjedoste“ naziva proročkom riječju i mačem duha te ih primjenjuje na **današnju Hrvatsku**. Podsjeća da se Gospa hrvatskom narodu ukazuje 45 godina. Umjesto da se narod ujedini oko **Gospe Kraljice mira** i oko riječi Božje, svi su protiv svih, a i u molitvenim zajednicama, upozorava, ima zavisti. To će trajati „dok nešto ne udari“, a tada će se pokazati što je Božje, a što ljudsko.

Riječi „evo, napuštena vam kuća“ tumači kao upozorenje: kad ljudi ne žele slušati riječ Božju, Bog ima i druge metode.

Završnu Isusovu rečenicu, „nećete me vidjeti dok ne reknete: Blagoslovljen onaj koji dolazi u ime Gospodnje“, Grebenar čita kao poruku da **nema mira dok se Isus ne prizna Sinom Božjim**. Bog, naglašava, neće prilagođavati svoju objavu ni tvrdokornim Židovima ni tvrdokornim Hrvatima koji ne žele prihvatiti obraćenje. Dao je ono što je dao: Međugorje i Crkvu. Svatko treba razlučivati i paziti kako sluša. Kad se ispuni vrijeme, zaključuje voditelj, nastupa nova faza.

magisterium.assessment: Odlomak ispravno ističe Isusovu žalost nad Jeruzalemom, poziv na obraćenje i biblijski primjer Ninive, ali zatim iz tog teksta izvodi nedovoljno utemeljene osude „lažne braće“ i tvrdnje o Hrvatskoj te budućem udaru. Govor o navodnim ukazanjima i „novoj fazi“ treba jasnije podrediti crkvenom razlučivanju i konačnosti Kristove objave.
concerns: Jonina priča potvrđuje da su se Ninivljani odazvali pozivu na obraćenje, ali ponuđeni tekstovi ne opravdavaju zaključak da su Židovi kao skupina odbili obraćenje niti etiketiranje vjernika kao „lažne braće“.

Primjena Isusove tužaljke nad Jeruzalemom na Hrvatsku može poslužiti kao opći poticaj na obraćenje, ali odlomak je predstavlja gotovo kao posebnu proročku osudu i najavljuje udar bez jasne biblijske ili crkvene potvrde. Biblijsko proroštvo prvenstveno razotkriva Božju volju za sadašnjost, a ne služi neutemeljenom predviđanju budućih događaja.

Tvrdnju da se Gospa hrvatskom narodu ukazuje 45 godina ne treba iznositi kao utvrđenu nadnaravnu činjenicu bez odgovarajućeg crkvenog razlučivanja. Privatne objave ne dopunjuju Kristovu konačnu objavu, nisu obvezatne za vjeru i trebaju voditi Kristu i Evanđelju.
Izraz da Bog, kada ga ljudi ne slušaju, ima „i druge metode“ može zvučati kao pripisivanje budućih nevolja izravnoj Božjoj kazni; odlomak ne daje dovoljno osnove za takvu konkretnu tvrdnju.
magisterium.enrichment: Isusove riječi o Jeruzalemu izražavaju istodobno njegovu ljubav prema gradu i bol zbog odbijanja proroka, pa ih je primjerenije čitati kao ozbiljan poziv na obraćenje nego kao blanketnu osudu naroda. Ninivljani su se obratili, a Bog je poštedio grad; ta je pripovijest naglašava milosrđe i stvarnu mogućnost promjene. Crkveno razlučivanje privatnih objava traži usmjerenost Kristu, suglasnost s vjerom i moralom te duhovne plodove; takve objave mogu pomagati živjeti Evanđelje, ali ga ne mogu zamijeniti niti mu dodati novu javnu objavu.

magisterium.assessment_en: The passage correctly highlights Jesus' sorrow over Jerusalem, the call to conversion, and the biblical example of Nineveh, but then from that text derives insufficiently grounded condemnations of "false brethren" and claims about Croatia and a future strike. Discourse on alleged apparitions and a "new phase" should be more clearly subordinated to ecclesial discernment and the definitiveness of Christ's revelation.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Jesus' words over Jerusalem express simultaneously his love for the city and grief over the rejection of the prophets, so it is more appropriate to read them as a serious call to conversion than as a blanket condemnation of the people. The Ninevites converted, and God spared the city; that narrative emphasizes mercy and the real possibility of change. Ecclesial discernment of private revelations requires orientation toward Christ, conformity with faith and morals, and spiritual fruits; such revelations can help live the Gospel, but cannot replace it or add a new public revelation to it.
concerns_en: Jonah's story confirms that the Ninevites responded to the call to conversion, but the provided texts do not justify the conclusion that the Jews as a group rejected conversion, nor labeling believers as "false brethren."

Applying Jesus' lament over Jerusalem to Croatia can serve as a general impetus for conversion, but the passage presents it almost as a special prophetic condemnation and announces a strike without clear biblical or ecclesial confirmation. Biblical prophecy primarily reveals God's will for the present, rather than serving unfounded predictions of future events.

The claim that Our Lady has been appearing to the Croatian people for 45 years should not be presented as an established supernatural fact without appropriate ecclesial discernment. Private revelations do not complement Christ's definitive revelation, are not mandatory for belief, and must lead to Christ and the Gospel.

The expression that God, when people do not listen to him, has "other methods as well" can sound like attributing future misfortunes to direct divine punishment; the passage does not provide sufficient basis for such a specific assertion.

sections.subtitle_en: Lament over Jerusalem and a view of today's Croatia
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host connects Jesus' lament over Jerusalem with Croatia and Međugorje
sections.content_en:
Jesus' harsh word over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets and stones those who are sent to it, the host interprets as a condemnation of the city to which God sent messengers. He compares it with the story of **Jonah**, whom God sent to pagan **Nineveh**. The Ninevites repented, while the Jewish believers did not, which Grebenar calls an example of "false brothers."

The words "how often would I have gathered your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing" he calls a prophetic word and a sword of the spirit and applies them to **today's Croatia**. He recalls that Our Lady has been appearing to the Croatian people for 45 years. Instead of the people uniting around **Our Lady Queen of Peace** and around the word of God, everyone is against everyone, and even in prayer communities, he warns, there is envy. That will last "until something strikes," and then it will be revealed what is of God and what is human.

The words "behold, your house is forsaken" he interprets as a warning: when people do not want to listen to the word of God, God has other methods as well.

The concluding sentence of Jesus, "you will not see me until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord," Grebenar reads as a message that **there is no peace until Jesus is recognized as the Son of God**. God, he emphasizes, will not adjust his revelation either to stubborn Jews or to stubborn Croats who do not want to accept conversion. He gave what he gave: Međugorje and the Church. Everyone needs to discern and watch how they listen. When the time is fulfilled, the host concludes, a new phase begins.

sections.subtitle: Poziv na članstvo i donacije: „Inicijativa iz naroda“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva gledatelje da postanu članovi i podrže domoljubnu inicijativu
sections.content:
Voditelj zatim upućuje poziv svim gledateljima i slušateljima da postanu **članovi domoljubne inicijative Ora et Labora**. Vezu s tumačenjem uspostavlja odmah: poziva ih da imaju „vjeru i povjerenje, a ne sumnju“.

Učlaniti se može preko web stranice inicijative, a uz to su navedeni brojevi mobitela za dodatne informacije, posebno i za Bosnu i Hercegovinu.

Poziva i na **financijske donacije**. Inicijativu opisuje kao „vašu inicijativu“, kao pokret iz naroda, „od ostatka koji se piše velikim slovima“. Cilj joj je, kaže, da se čuje riječ Božja i da se prenese riječ istine o svim područjima ljudskog života.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na članstvo i donacije za inicijativu koja želi širiti Božju riječ i istinu može biti u skladu s kršćanskim sudjelovanjem u javnom životu, ali sam opis ne daje dovoljno podataka da bi se procijenili njezini konkretni ciljevi, djelovanje i upravljanje donacijama. Povezivanje povjerenja s odbacivanjem sumnje zahtijeva oprez: kršćansko povjerenje ne isključuje razborito provjeravanje tvrdnji i djelovanja.
concerns: Izraz „ostatak koji se piše velikim slovima” može zvučati kao da se konkretna inicijativa poistovjećuje s biblijskim „ostatkom”; bez dodatnog konteksta nije moguće utvrditi misli li se na to, ali takvu tvrdnju ne bi trebalo pretpostavljati.

Poziv na vjeru i povjerenje ne bi smio obeshrabrivati legitimna pitanja o nauku, ciljevima, financijskoj transparentnosti ili političkom djelovanju inicijative. Katolici trebaju prosuđivati javne inicijative prema Evanđelju i cjelovitom moralnom i društvenom nauku Crkve.
magisterium.enrichment: Katolički nauk potiče vjernike da sudjeluju u javnom životu i rade za opće dobro, ali i da političke prijedloge i društveno djelovanje prosuđuju u svjetlu Evanđelja. Vjera u Krista kao Put, Istinu i Život poziva na svjedočenje istine, dok katolički nauk istodobno upozorava da se vjera ne smije koristiti za usmjeravanje savjesti prema isključivo zemaljskoj, utopijskoj nadi. Biblijski govor o „ostatku” pripada kontekstu povijesti spasenja i sam po sebi ne potvrđuje posebnu suvremenu organizaciju ili pokret.

magisterium.assessment_en: The call for membership and donations for an initiative that aims to spread the Word of God and truth can be in accordance with Christian participation in public life, but the description itself does not provide enough data to evaluate its concrete goals, activities, and management of donations. Linking trust with the rejection of doubt requires caution: Christian trust does not exclude prudent verification of claims and actions.
magisterium.enrichment_en: Catholic teaching encourages the faithful to participate in public life and work for the common good, but also to judge political proposals and social engagement in the light of the Gospel. Faith in Christ as the Way, the Truth, and the Life calls for witnessing to the truth, while Catholic teaching simultaneously warns that faith must not be used to direct consciences toward an exclusively earthly, utopian hope. Biblical discourse on the "remnant" belongs to the context of salvation history and does not in itself validate a specific contemporary organization or movement.
concerns_en: The expression "remnant capitalized" can sound as though the specific initiative is equated with the biblical "remnant"; without additional context it is not possible to establish whether that is meant, but such a claim should not be assumed.

The call to faith and trust should not discourage legitimate questions about doctrine, goals, financial transparency, or political action of the initiative. Catholics should evaluate public initiatives according to the Gospel and the complete moral and social teaching of the Church.

sections.subtitle_en: Call for membership and donations: "An initiative from the people"
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invites viewers to become members and support the patriotic initiative
sections.content_en:
The host then extends an invitation to all viewers and listeners to become **members of the patriotic initiative Ora et Labora**. He establishes the connection with the interpretation immediately: he invites them to have "faith and trust, and not doubt."

One can join via the initiative's website, and mobile phone numbers for additional information are listed alongside, specifically also for Bosnia and Herzegovina.

He also appeals for **financial donations**. He describes the initiative as "your initiative," as a movement from the people, "from the remnant that is written with capital letters." Its goal, he says, is for the word of God to be heard and for the word of truth to be conveyed regarding all areas of human life.

sections.subtitle: Svjedočanstvo Branke: rana koja je zacijelila nakon molitve
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj čita Brankino svjedočanstvo o ozdravljenju supruga
sections.content:
Voditelj čita svjedočanstvo **Branke**, koja zahvaljuje Isusu za milosti primljene tijekom **tridesetodnevnice Krvi Kristove**. Njezin suprug imao je na licu ranu koja nije zarastala. Potvrđeno je da je tumorskog porijekla, pa je operativno uklonjena. Nedavno mu se na ramenu pojavila nova mala rana koja također nije zarastala. Branka je u molitvi zavapila Isusu da ozdravi supruga i stavila ruku na ranu. Nakon dva dana krasta je, kako piše, poprimila oblik malog srca, a nekoliko dana kasnije otpala je i rana je zacijelila.

Voditelj to svjedočanstvo povezuje s nedavnim iskustvom. Jedna žena iz Hercegovine, koju poznaje otprije i poslovno, zamolila ga je da se pomoli za muža koji je upravo izašao s operacije. Dok ga je predavao u molitvi, došlo mu je da ta žena treba **položiti ruku na svoga muža i moliti za njega**, jer će milost izaći preko njezinih ruku. Supružnici su, objašnjava, jedno tijelo i jedan duh i smiju polagati ruke jedno na drugo. Naglašava da Brankino svjedočanstvo prije toga nije pročitao.

Iz toga izvodi poruku o snazi bračne ljubavi: žena čije je srce u Isusu može muža ozdraviti, obratiti i učiniti drugom osobom. Može ga, kaže, učiniti „vrhunskim čovjekom“, ali ga može i uništiti.

magisterium.assessment: Molitva za bolesnog supružnika i svjedočenje o primljenoj milosti mogu biti u skladu s katoličkom vjerom, koja priznaje mogućnost Božjeg čudesnog djelovanja, ali i naglašava razborito prosuđivanje takvih tvrdnji te trajnu važnost liječenja. Odlomak postaje teološki nejasan kada govori kao da žena svojim polaganjem ruku može ozdraviti ili preobraziti muža, jer to može zasjeniti Božju slobodu i muževu osobnu slobodu.
concerns: Tvrdnja da će milost „izaći preko njezinih ruku” može zvučati kao da polaganje ruku samo po sebi prenosi ozdravljenje; katolički govor trebao bi jasno prikazati molitvu kao prošnju Bogu, a ne kao zajamčenu tehniku ili moć osobe.
Osobno svjedočanstvo da je rana zacijelila nakon molitve nije samo po sebi dokaz čudesnog ozdravljenja; Crkva takve tvrdnje prosuđuje oprezno, a molitva ne zamjenjuje medicinsku skrb.

Izraz da žena može muža „učiniti” vrhunskim čovjekom ili ga uništiti pretjerano pripisuje supružnici moć nad njegovom promjenom i može zvučati kao da je odgovorna za njegovu svetost, obraćenje ili propast.
magisterium.enrichment: Crkva priznaje da Bog može djelovati na izvanredan način i da su apostoli bili povezani s Isusovom službom ozdravljanja, ali istodobno naglašava razborito prosuđivanje takvih događaja i obvezu skrbi za bolesne. Supružnikova iskrena ljubav, strpljenje i ustrajna molitva mogu pripremiti drugoga za obraćenje, no obraćenje ostaje slobodan odgovor osobe na Božju milost, a ne nešto što jedan supružnik može proizvesti ili nametnuti.
magisterium.assessment_en: Prayer for a sick spouse and testimony of received grace can be in accordance with the Catholic faith, which recognizes the possibility of God's miraculous intervention, but also emphasizes prudent discernment of such claims and the enduring importance of medical treatment. The passage becomes theologically unclear when it speaks as though a wife through her laying on of hands can heal or transform her husband, because that can overshadow God's freedom and the husband's personal freedom.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Church recognizes that God can act in an extraordinary way and that the apostles were linked with Jesus' ministry of healing, but at the same time emphasizes prudent discernment of such events and the obligation to care for the sick. A spouse's sincere love, patience, and persevering prayer can prepare the other for conversion, but conversion remains a person's free response to God's grace, not something one spouse can produce or impose.
concerns_en: The claim that grace will "come out through her hands" can sound as though the laying on of hands in itself transmits healing; Catholic discourse should clearly depict prayer as a petition to God, and not as a guaranteed technique or power of the person.
Personal testimony that a wound healed after prayer is not in itself proof of miraculous healing; the Church evaluates such claims cautiously, and prayer does not replace medical care.

The expression that a wife can "make" her husband a top-tier man or destroy him excessively attributes to the spouse power over his transformation and can sound as though she is responsible for his sanctity, conversion, or ruin.

sections.subtitle_en: Branka's testimony: a wound that healed after prayer
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host reads Branka's testimony about the healing of her husband
sections.content_en:
The host reads the testimony of **Branka**, who thanks Jesus for the graces received during the **thirty-day devotion to the Blood of Christ**. Her husband had a wound on his face that would not heal. It was confirmed to be of tumorous origin, so it was surgically removed. Recently, a new small wound appeared on his shoulder that also would not heal. Branka cried out in prayer to Jesus to heal her husband and placed her hand on the wound. After two days the scab, as she writes, took the shape of a small heart, and a few days later it fell off and the wound healed.

The host connects that testimony with a recent experience. A woman from Hercegovina, whom he knows from before and through business, asked him to pray for her husband who had just come out of surgery. While he was commending him in prayer, it came to him that this woman should **lay her hand on her husband and pray for him**, because the grace would come out through her hands. Spouses, he explains, are one body and one spirit and are allowed to lay hands on one another. He emphasizes that he had not read Branka's testimony before that.

From this he derives a message about the power of marital love: a woman whose heart is in Jesus can heal her husband, convert him, and make him a different person. She can, he says, make him a "top-quality man," but she can also destroy him.
keywords_en: thirty-day devotion to the Blood of Christ

sections.subtitle: „Budi muško, a ne Dugouško“: krunica na trgovima i završni blagoslov
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva na javnu molitvu krunice na trgovima uz šaljivu usporedbu s Duškom Dugouškom
sections.content:
Pred kraj emisije voditelj se obraća **Hrvatima izvan domovine**, iz Njemačke, Austrije i šire, i upućuje na brojeve mobitela u Njemačkoj preko kojih se organizira dolazak na **javnu molitvu krunice na trgu u Zagrebu**. Poziv proširuje i na sve koji žive po hrvatskim gradovima: neka pokrenu molitvu krunice na trgu u svom mjestu, općini ili gradu.

Poruku izriče šaljivo i izravno: **„Budi hrabar, budi muško, a ne Dugouško.“** Starijim gledateljima, kaže, jasno je na što misli, na Duška Dugouška, strašljivog zeca iz crtića.

Emisija se zaključuje blagoslovom u ime Oca i Sina i Duha Svetoga, uz zazivanje Majke Božje s Isusom i svetim Josipom. Voditelj podsjeća i da se narudžbom prve, druge i treće knjige **„Isus Lider“** pomaže dovršetak **međunarodnog edukacijskog centra Kraljica Mira u Međugorju**. Zahvaljuje svima koji su već kupili knjige i poziva one koji osjećaju poticaj da pomognu dovršiti centar. Odjavljuje se pozivom da se Ora et Labora prati svaki dan, „na veću slavu Božju“.

magisterium.assessment: Poziv na javnu molitvu krunice, poticaj na hrabrost te završno zazivanje Boga i Svete obitelji u osnovi su usklađeni s katoličkom pobožnošću; krunica je molitva usredotočena na Kristova otajstva i moljena u duhovnom zajedništvu s Marijom. Izraz „budi muško, a ne Dugouško“ nije sam po sebi naukovna tvrdnja, ali može nepotrebno poistovjetiti hrabrost s muškim identitetom i ismijati plašljivost.
concerns: Šaljiva dosjetka može sugerirati da su hrabrost i zauzimanje za vjeru osobine koje pripadaju samo muškarcima; kršćanska hrabrost poziv je svakom vjerniku.
Iz opisa nije jasno izgovara li voditelj blagoslov kao molitveni zaziv Božje zaštite ili kao službeni liturgijski blagoslov; ne treba pretpostaviti da je riječ o ovom drugom.
magisterium.enrichment: Krunica nije tek javni znak pripadnosti ili hrabrosti, nego razmatranje Kristova života s Marijom; njezina je svrha voditi vjernike Kristu. Marija i sveti Josip mogu se zazivati kao uzori vjernosti i povjerenja u Boga, dok svaki poziv na molitvu treba ostaviti prostor za slobodno sudjelovanje i poštovanje dostojanstva svih vjernika.
magisterium.assessment_en: The call to public prayer of the Rosary, encouragement to courage, and the final invocation of God and the Holy Family are fundamentally aligned with Catholic devotion; the Rosary is a prayer centered on Christ's mysteries and prayed in spiritual communion with Mary. The expression "be a man, not a Bugs Bunny" is not in itself a doctrinal claim, but can unnecessarily equate courage with male identity and mock timidity.
magisterium.enrichment_en: The Rosary is not merely a public sign of belonging or courage, but contemplation of Christ's life with Mary; its purpose is to lead believers to Christ. Mary and Saint Joseph can be invoked as models of fidelity and trust in God, while every call to prayer should leave room for free participation and respect for the dignity of all believers.
concerns_en: A humorous quip can suggest that courage and standing up for the faith are attributes belonging only to men; Christian courage is a call to every believer.

From the description it is not clear whether the host pronounces the blessing as a prayerful invocation of God's protection or as an official liturgical blessing; one should not assume it is the latter.

sections.subtitle_en: "Be a man, not a Bugs Bunny": the rosary in public squares and final blessing
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invites to public prayer of the rosary in town squares with a humorous comparison to Bugs Bunny
sections.content_en:
Toward the end of the broadcast, the host addresses **Croats outside the homeland**, from Germany, Austria, and beyond, and refers to mobile phone numbers in Germany through which arrival at the **public prayer of the rosary on the square in Zagreb** is organized. He extends the invitation to all who live in Croatian cities as well: let them start the prayer of the rosary on the square in their town, municipality, or city.

He states the message humorously and directly: **"Be brave, be a man, and not a Dugouško."** To older viewers, he says, it is clear what he means, Duško Dugouško, the fearful rabbit from the cartoon.

The broadcast concludes with a blessing in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit, invoking the Mother of God with Jesus and Saint Joseph. The host also reminds that ordering the first, second, and third books of **"Jesus the Leader"** helps complete the **Queen of Peace international educational center in Međugorje**. He thanks all who have already purchased the books and invites those who feel a prompting to help complete the center. He signs off with an invitation to follow Ora et Labora every day, "for the greater glory of God."

iterations.theme_en: Interpretation of the whole armor of God (Eph 6), interpretation of the gospel about Herod and Jerusalem, and announcements, testimony, and blessing
